definition_zh: 正确的；右边的；权利；正好
definition_en: correct, on the right side, a just claim, or exactly
core_image: 路口亮起绿灯后向右转的人
scene: 她在路口向右转，很快就找到了那家书店。She turned right at the corner and soon found the bookshop.
sceneCN: 这里 right 是「右边」（第 2 个义项：朝向右侧的方向）；句意：她在路口向右转，很快就找到了那家书店。

senses.title: Correct
senses.definition: true or correct
senses.definitionCN: 真实或正确的
senses.example: You gave the right answer.
senses.exampleCN: 你给出了正确答案。
senses.why: What is straight is also what is true.
senses.whyCN: 笔直的东西也就是正确的东西。

senses.title: The right side
senses.definition: the side opposite the left
senses.definitionCN: 与左边相对的一侧
senses.example: The bank is on your right.
senses.exampleCN: 银行在你的右边。
senses.why: The strong hand side came to be called right.
senses.whyCN: 有力的那只手所在一侧被称为右边。

senses.title: A just claim
senses.definition: something you are morally or legally allowed to have
senses.definitionCN: 在道德或法律上可以拥有的事物
senses.example: Everyone has the right to speak.
senses.exampleCN: 每个人都有说话的权利。
senses.why: A straight rule protects a just claim.
senses.whyCN: 正直的规则保护正当的诉求。

senses.title: Exactly
senses.definition: exactly or directly
senses.definitionCN: 恰好或径直
senses.example: The book is right here.
senses.exampleCN: 书就在这儿。
senses.why: A straight line reaches exactly where it aims.
senses.whyCN: 直线正好抵达它指向的地方。

intro.en: Right comes from Old English riht, straight, just or true.
intro.cn: right 源自古英语 riht，意为笔直、公正或真实。

items.en: Riht means straight and just.
items.cn: riht 意为笔直与公正。

items.en: Straight becomes correct and right.
items.cn: 笔直引申为正确与正当。

items.en: The right hand gives the side sense.
items.cn: 右手义给出了方位义。

items.en: Rights become legal claims.
items.cn: rights 成为法律上的权利。

items.en: Right now and right away add exactness.
items.cn: right now 与 right away 增加了确切义。

note.en: Right is correct or the right side; rightly means with good reason.
note.cn: right 指正确或右边，rightly 意为有正当理由地。

normalIntro.en: Right begins as straight, and straight becomes correct.
normalIntro.cn: right 最初表示笔直，笔直引申为正确。

normal.en: The right answer is the correct one.
normal.cn: right answer 就是正确的答案。

normal.en: Your right hand is on the right side.
normal.cn: 你的右手就在右边。

normal.en: A right is a just claim.
normal.cn: right 是一种正当诉求。

normal.en: Right now means at this very moment.
normal.cn: right now 意为就在此刻。

normal.en: Rightly means with good reason.
normal.cn: rightly 意为有正当理由地。

abstract.en: Picture a line drawn perfectly straight.
abstract.cn: 想象一条画得笔直的线。

abstract.en: Imagine a hand raised to claim a fair share.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手举起，要求公平的一份。

abstract.en: Think of an arrow pointing exactly at the dot.
abstract.cn: 想象一支箭正好指向圆点。

examples.en: Is this the right way to the station?
examples.cn: 去车站是走这条路吗？

examples.en: She writes with her right hand.
examples.cn: 她用右手写字。

examples.en: Children have the right to learn.
examples.cn: 儿童有学习的权利。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「right」听起来像「直」——笔直、正确，也指向右手那一边。

root: 古英语 riht（笔直、公正）→ 正确、右边、权利，核心义「笔直不分叉的，因而正当」。

sensesIntro.en: Right means correct, the right-hand side, a just claim, or exactly.
sensesIntro.cn: right 意为正确、右边、权利，或正好。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a straight line with no bend.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条笔直不弯的线。

branches.en: Straightness turns into correctness.
branches.cn: 笔直引申为正确。

branches.en: The right hand gives the side word.
branches.cn: 右手给出了方位词。

branches.en: A just claim is a moral straight line.
branches.cn: 正当诉求是一条道德上的直线。

branches.en: Exactly is the straight line hitting its mark.
branches.cn: 正好就是直线命中目标。

branches.en: Correct and just both come from straightness.
branches.cn: 正确与公正都来自笔直。

intro.en: Right is a native English word from Old English riht.
intro.cn: right 是源自古英语 riht 的英语本族词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin cousin rectus, straight, appears in correct and direct.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语近亲 rectus（笔直）出现在 correct 与 direct 中。

items.exampleCN: 复数形式常指各项权利。
rectus 出现在 correct 中。

latinEntries.example: Rectus is the Latin cousin of right.
latinEntries.exampleCN: rectus 是 right 的拉丁近亲。

definition_zh: 戒指；环形物；铃声；给……打电话；响铃
definition_en: a circle of metal worn as jewelry, a circular shape, a sound of a bell, or to call someone by phone
core_image: 一圈首尾相接的圆环：戴在手上是戒指，敲响是铃声，接通是电话
scene: 生日那天他送给她一枚戒指，她高兴得直笑。He gave her a beautiful ring for her birthday, and she smiled with joy.
sceneCN: 这里 ring 是「戒指」（第 1 个义项：戴在手上的环形首饰）；句意：生日那天他送给她一枚漂亮的戒指，她笑得很开心。

pos.zh: 响铃；按铃；打电话；成环形

derivatives.zh: 由动词加 -er 后缀构成，指按铃的人或声音极像的人
由现在分词转形容词，义为「响亮的；响个不停的」
由 ear 加 ring 构成的合成词，义为「耳环」

senses.title: A band of jewelry
senses.definition: a piece of jewelry shaped like a circle that you wear on your finger
senses.definitionCN: 戴在手指上的环形首饰
senses.example: She wears a gold ring on her finger.
senses.exampleCN: 她手指上戴着一枚金戒指。
senses.why: The circle shape of metal around a finger is the oldest image of the word.
senses.whyCN: 金属围成一个圈戴在手上，是这个词最古老、最直观的画面。

senses.title: A circular shape
senses.definition: any object or area shaped like a circle
senses.definitionCN: 任何圆形的物体或区域
senses.example: The children danced in a ring.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们围成一圈跳舞。
senses.why: The shape itself extends beyond jewelry to anything round and closed.
senses.whyCN: 圆环的形状从首饰延伸到一切首尾相接的圆形物体或区域。

senses.title: A ringing sound
senses.definition: the sound made by a bell or a phone
senses.definitionCN: 铃或电话发出的声音
senses.example: There was a ring at the door.
senses.exampleCN: 门铃响了。
senses.why: A bell is shaped like a ring, and its repeated sound became the name of the sound.
senses.whyCN: 钟铃形似圆环，其反复震响的声音也被借用来指铃声本身。

senses.title: To make a bell sound
senses.definition: to cause a bell to make a sound
senses.definitionCN: 使铃发出声音
senses.example: Someone is ringing the doorbell.
senses.exampleCN: 有人在按门铃。
senses.why: Once the sound is named, the action that produces it takes the same word.
senses.whyCN: 声音有了名字，发出这种声音的动作也顺理成章地用同一个词。

senses.title: To call by phone
senses.definition: to telephone someone, especially in British English
senses.definitionCN: 给某人打电话，英式英语常用
senses.example: I will ring you tonight.
senses.exampleCN: 我今晚给你打电话。
senses.why: Early telephones rang a bell when called, so the bell action transferred to phone calls.
senses.whyCN: 早期电话靠摇铃呼叫，铃的动作自然转移到打电话这件事上。

intro.en: Ring comes from Old English hring, meaning a circle or something bent into a loop.
intro.cn: ring 源自古英语 hring，意为圆环或弯成圈状之物。

items.en: The reconstructed Germanic root *hringaz means a circle or curved band.
items.cn: 重构的日耳曼语词根 *hringaz 意为圆圈或弯曲的环带，一般认为这是该词的共同源头。

items.en: Hring in Old English already meant both a circular band and jewelry.
items.cn: 古英语 hring 已兼指环形物与环形首饰，戒指义从一开始就存在。

items.en: The verb sense of making a bell sound appears from the sound of struck metal.
items.cn: 动词「鸣响」义来自敲击金属时绕梁的余音，与铃声的反复回荡相关，属拟声性引申。

items.en: Ring keeps the circle senses and gains the bell sense.
items.cn: 中古英语时期 ring 保留圆环各义项，并固定下钟铃响声义。

items.en: The telephone brings a new use: to ring someone up means to call them.
items.cn: 电话机发明后，ring 的新用法诞生：ring someone up 即给某人打电话。

items.en: British English keeps ring for phone calls, while American English prefers call.
items.cn: 英式英语沿用 ring 表示打电话，美式英语更常用 call，形成今天的地区差异。

note.en: Ring has look-alike words about circles and near-meaning words about sounds and calls.
note.cn: ring 的形近词多与圆形相关，近义词则集中在声音与打电话的义场。

entries.definition: a small ring-shaped curl of hair
entries.definitionCN: 小卷发；小环，由 ring 加指小后缀构成，与 ring 同源
溜冰场，拼写相近且读音略同，但词源与圆环无关，只是形近
拧；绞，读音与 ring 完全相同但拼写多一个 w，词源不同，需靠语境区分

entries.definition: a perfectly round shape or a group arranged in a round form
entries.definitionCN: 圆；圈子，泛指圆形与围成的圈，不特指首饰
打电话，美式英语的常用说法，与英式 ring 相对

entries.definition: to make a clear ringing sound like a bell
entries.definitionCN: 鸣响；敲出清脆的钟声，强调悦耳的乐音而非铃的动作

normalIntro.en: Five ways to remember ring through its shape and sound.
normalIntro.cn: 五条围绕圆环形状与铃声的记忆路径。

normal.en: RING has a circular G at the end, like the ring itself closing into a loop.
normal.cn: RING 结尾的 G 圆圆的，就像戒指首尾相接的小圆环。

normal.en: A wedding ring goes on the r-ight f-inger: R + ING.
normal.cn: 婚戒戴在「right（右手）」的手指上：R 加 ING 就是戒指。

normal.en: The phone RINGS: ring-ring is the sound itself, so the word imitates the bell.
normal.cn: 电话铃「ring-ring」响，这个拟声式的叠音就是铃声本身。

normal.en: EAR + RING = earring, the same circle moved to the ear.
normal.cn: 耳朵加圆环就是耳环 earring，同一只圆环换了个位置。

normal.en: Boxing RING is a square but the fighters are enclosed in a circle of ropes.
normal.cn: 拳击台叫 ring，虽然台子是方的，但四周被围绳圈住，保留了「围成圈」的古义。

abstract.en: Imagine a golden circle floating in the air, waiting to be worn.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚金色圆环悬浮空中，等待有人把它戴上。

abstract.en: Hear the bell echo in circles, each sound wave a smaller ring.
abstract.cn: 听钟声一圈圈荡开，每一道声波都是一枚缩小的小圆环。

abstract.en: A phone call draws a ring that connects two people across distance.
abstract.cn: 一通电话画出一道圆环，把相隔两地的两个人连在一起。

examples.en: He slipped the ring onto her finger.
examples.cn: 他把戒指轻轻套上她的手指。

examples.en: Please ring me when you arrive at the station.
examples.cn: 你到车站后请给我打电话。

examples.en: The church bells ring every Sunday morning.
examples.cn: 教堂的钟每星期天早晨都会敲响。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「锐赢」——戴着亮闪闪的戒指去比赛，锐气逼人，赢面大增；ring 读音近似「锐赢」

root: 一般认为源自日耳曼语词根 *hringaz（圆环、弯曲的环带），古英语 hring 直承此义；动词鸣响义属拟声性引申，与圆环名词同形但来源路径不同。

sensesIntro.en: Ring moves from a circular band of metal to any circle, then to bell sounds and phone calls.
sensesIntro.cn: ring 从金属圆环出发，扩展到一切圈状物，再引申出铃声与打电话等义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a closed circle of metal
core.cn: 核心意象：一枚首尾相接的金属圆环

branches.en: The circle shape covers both finger jewelry and any round arrangement.
branches.cn: 圆环形状同时覆盖手指首饰与一切圈状排列。

branches.en: The repeated clang of a bell becomes the name of the sound.
branches.cn: 钟铃反复的敲击声被用作声音本身的名称。

branches.en: The action of making a bell sound takes the same word.
branches.cn: 使铃发声的动作沿用同一个词。

branches.en: Early telephones rang bells, so calling someone became ringing them.
branches.cn: 早期电话靠铃声呼叫，打电话由此借用了响铃的说法。

branches.en: Jewelry and bells share the metal circle: same shape, different use.
branches.cn: 首饰与钟铃共享金属圆环这一形状：同形而用途不同。

intro.en: Ring forms compounds and derivatives around its circle shape and bell sound.
intro.cn: ring 的构词围绕圆环形状与铃声两条线索展开。

latinIntro.en: Ring is a Germanic word without Latin relatives, so no Latin entries are listed.
latinIntro.cn: ring 属日耳曼语源词，没有拉丁同族词，故不列拉丁词条。

items.example: She bought a pair of pearl earrings.

items.meaning: the finger that wears a wedding ring
items.meaningCN: 无名指；戴戒指的是第四根手指
items.example: In China the wedding ring goes on the left ring finger.
items.exampleCN: 在中国婚戒戴在左手无名指上。

items.meaning: the enclosed area where boxers fight
items.meaningCN: 拳击台，古义「围成圈」的保留
items.example: The champion stepped into the boxing ring.

items.meaning: a road that circles a city
items.example: Take the ring road to avoid the downtown traffic.
items.exampleCN: 走环城公路避开市中心的拥堵。

items.meaning: a person or thing that rings
items.example: The ringer of the bell is the oldest student.
items.exampleCN: 敲钟的是年纪最大的学生。

items.meaningCN: 响亮的； ringing 作形容词表示声音洪亮

items.meaning: the area right next to a boxing ring
items.example: They had ringside seats for the match.
items.exampleCN: 他们坐到了比赛的正前排座位。

items.meaning: a small ring that holds keys
items.example: My key ring holds five keys.
items.exampleCN: 我的钥匙环上挂着五把钥匙。

items.example: His promise did not ring true.
items.exampleCN: 他的承诺听上去不太可信。

items.meaning: to record a sale on a cash register; to phone
items.meaningCN: 把款项记入收银机；打电话
items.example: The clerk rang up the purchase.
items.exampleCN: 店员把货款记入了收银机。

definition_en: to move upward, stand up, or increase; also the act of rising
core_image: 海面上缓缓升起的太阳
scene: 太阳从海面上升起，渔船陆续出海。The sun rose over the sea and the boats set out.
sceneCN: 这里 rise 是「升起」（第 1 个义项：向上移动）；句意：太阳从海面上升起，渔船陆续出海。

senses.title: Moving upward
senses.definition: to move from a lower place to a higher one
senses.definitionCN: 从较低处移到较高处
senses.example: Smoke rose from the chimney.
senses.exampleCN: 烟从烟囱里升起。
senses.why: The core act is simple upward movement.
senses.whyCN: 核心动作就是单纯的向上移动。

senses.title: Standing up
senses.definition: to get up from sitting or lying
senses.definitionCN: 从坐卧状态起身
senses.example: Everyone rose when the judge entered.
senses.exampleCN: 法官进来时大家都站了起来。
senses.why: Standing lifts the body upward.
senses.whyCN: 站立就是把身体向上抬起。

senses.title: An increase
senses.definition: an increase in amount or level
senses.definitionCN: 数量或水平的增加
senses.example: There was a sharp rise in prices.
senses.exampleCN: 物价急剧上涨。
senses.why: A number that goes up is also rising.
senses.whyCN: 数字向上走也是上升。

senses.title: A beginning
senses.definition: the start or cause of something
senses.definitionCN: 某事物的开端或原因
senses.example: The quarrel gave rise to a long feud.
senses.exampleCN: 这场争吵引发了长期的仇怨。
senses.why: Things rise from a source, as smoke from fire.
senses.whyCN: 事物从源头升起，就像烟从火起。

intro.en: Rise comes from Old English rīsan, to rise or get up.
intro.cn: rise 源自古英语 rīsan，意为升起或起身。

items.en: Rīsan means to rise.
items.cn: rīsan 意为升起。

items.en: The sun and smoke both rise.
items.cn: 太阳与烟都会升起。

items.en: Prices begin to rise in trade talk.
items.cn: 贸易语境中价格开始上涨。

items.en: Give rise to means cause.
items.cn: give rise to 意为引起。

items.en: Rise stays irregular: rise, rose, risen.
items.cn: rise 保持不规则变化：rise、rose、risen。

note.en: Rise does not take an object; raise needs one.
note.cn: rise 不带宾语，raise 需要带宾语。

normalIntro.en: Rise is the upward line of smoke or sun.
normalIntro.cn: rise 就是烟或太阳向上的那条线。

normal.en: The sun rises in the east.
normal.cn: the sun rises 太阳从东方升起。

normal.en: Rise up means get up or fight back.
normal.cn: rise up 意为起身或反抗。

normal.en: A sharp rise means a fast increase.
normal.cn: a sharp rise 意为快速上涨。

normal.en: Give rise to means cause something.
normal.cn: give rise to 意为引起某事。

normal.en: Rise above means go beyond a problem.
normal.cn: rise above 意为超越问题。

abstract.en: Picture a red sun lifting off the water.
abstract.cn: 想象一轮红日从水面升起。

abstract.en: Imagine smoke curling up a cold chimney.
abstract.cn: 想象烟从冰冷的烟囱里卷上去。

abstract.en: Think of a graph line climbing to the right.
abstract.cn: 想象一条折线向右上方攀升。

examples.en: Prices rose by ten percent last year.
examples.cn: 去年物价上涨了百分之十。

examples.en: She rose to answer the question.
examples.cn: 她站起来回答问题。

examples.en: The plan gave rise to many doubts.
examples.cn: 这个计划引起了诸多疑虑。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「rise」听起来像「拉起」——被拉起来，就是上升。

root: 古英语 rīsan（升起）→ rise，核心义「自下而上移动」，从太阳、身体到物价与起因都能延伸。

sensesIntro.en: Rise means to go up, to stand, to increase, or to begin from a source.
sensesIntro.cn: rise 意为向上、起身、增长，或从某处起源。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an upward line against the sky.
core.cn: 核心意象：天空下一条向上的线。

branches.en: Simple upward movement is the core.
branches.cn: 单纯的向上移动是核心。

branches.en: Standing raises the body from a chair.
branches.cn: 站起是把身体从椅子上抬起。

branches.en: Numbers that grow follow the same line.
branches.cn: 增长的数字沿着同样的线。

branches.en: A source sends things upward like smoke.
branches.cn: 源头把事物像烟一样向上送出。

branches.en: Physical and numeric rising share one image.
branches.cn: 物理上升与数字上涨共享同一个意象。

intro.en: Rise is a native irregular verb from Old English rīsan.
intro.cn: rise 是源自古英语 rīsan 的英语本族不规则动词。

latinIntro.en: The word is Germanic; ar- in arise is its closest prefix.
latinIntro.cn: 该词属于日耳曼语，arise 中的 ar- 是它最接近的前缀。

items.exampleCN: arise 是 rise 加 a-。

definition_en: the chance that something bad will happen, or to put something in danger
core_image: 不顾坏天气出发的登山者
scene: 登山者不顾天气变坏，冒着被困山中的风险出发。The climbers set off despite the weather, risking being trapped.
sceneCN: 这里 risk 是「冒…的风险」（第 3 个义项：把某事置于危险之中）；句意：登山者不顾天气变坏，冒着被困山中的风险出发。

senses.title: Chance of harm
senses.definition: the possibility that something bad will happen
senses.definitionCN: 坏事发生的可能性
senses.example: There is a risk of heavy rain tonight.
senses.exampleCN: 今晚有大雨的风险。
senses.why: The noun names the chance of loss before it comes.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词指损失尚未发生前的可能性。

senses.title: A dangerous person or thing
senses.definition: someone or something likely to cause harm
senses.definitionCN: 可能造成伤害的人或事物
senses.example: That old bridge is a risk to traffic.
senses.exampleCN: 那座旧桥对交通是个隐患。
senses.why: A risk can be the source, not only the chance.
senses.whyCN: 风险也可以指源头，而不只是可能性。

senses.title: To put in danger
senses.definition: to do something that may cause loss or harm
senses.definitionCN: 做可能带来损失或伤害的事
senses.example: He risked his job to help her.
senses.exampleCN: 他冒着丢掉工作的风险去帮她。
senses.why: The verb makes the chance personal and active.
senses.whyCN: 动词让这种可能性变得个人化且主动。

intro.en: Risk comes from French risque, probably from Italian risco, danger.
intro.cn: risk 源自法语 risque，可能来自意大利语 risco（危险）。

items.en: Risco means danger or bold chance.
items.cn: risco 意为危险或大胆的冒险。

items.en: Risque carries the word into French.
items.cn: risque 把词带入法语。

items.en: Risk enters English as a noun of chance.
items.cn: risk 以表示可能性的名词进入英语。

items.en: Insurance and health give it new uses.
items.cn: 保险与健康领域赋予它新用法。

items.en: The verb risk grows beside the noun.
items.cn: 动词 risk 与名词并行发展。

note.en: A risk is a chance of loss; a danger is the harm itself.
note.cn: risk 是损失的几率，danger 是伤害本身。

normalIntro.en: Risk is the shadow of a bad outcome.
normalIntro.cn: risk 是坏结果的影子。

normal.en: At risk means in danger.
normal.cn: at risk 意为处于危险中。

normal.en: Take a risk means accept a chance of loss.
normal.cn: take a risk 意为接受损失的可能。

normal.en: A health risk may hurt your body.
normal.cn: health risk 可能伤害身体。

normal.en: Risk of failure is the chance of failing.
normal.cn: risk of failure 是失败的可能。

normal.en: To risk your life is to put it in danger.
normal.cn: risk your life 就是把生命置于危险中。

abstract.en: Picture a thin bridge over a deep valley.
abstract.cn: 想象一座横跨深谷的细桥。

abstract.en: Imagine stepping onto thin ice in spring.
abstract.cn: 想象春天踩上薄冰。

abstract.en: Think of a coin thrown into the dark.
abstract.cn: 想象把一枚硬币扔进黑暗。

examples.en: Smoking increases the risk of illness.
examples.cn: 吸烟会增加患病的风险。

examples.en: They risked everything for the farm.
examples.cn: 他们为农场冒了一切风险。

examples.en: The children are at risk near the river.
examples.cn: 孩子们在河边很危险。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「risk」听起来像「锐思刻」——反复思量那一刻的危险，就是风险。

root: 意大利语 risco（危险）→ 法语 risque → risk，核心义「坏事发生前的可能，以及主动迎向它的行动」。

sensesIntro.en: Risk means the chance of harm, a source of harm, or to put something in danger.
sensesIntro.cn: risk 意为受害的可能、危险的源头，或使某物陷入危险。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thin bridge over a deep drop.
core.cn: 核心意象：深谷上的一座细桥。

branches.en: The chance of loss is the main sense.
branches.cn: 损失的可能性是主要义项。

branches.en: A dangerous thing is a risk in itself.
branches.cn: 危险的事物本身就是风险。

branches.en: The verb makes someone face the chance.
branches.cn: 动词让人主动面对这种可能。

branches.en: Chance and source both wear the same word.
branches.cn: 可能与源头共用同一个词。

branches.en: To risk is to accept the chance of loss.
branches.cn: 冒险就是接受损失的可能。

intro.en: Risk is a Romance borrowing, from Italian and French.
intro.cn: risk 是来自意大利语与法语的罗曼语借词。

latinIntro.en: Italian risco is the earliest known form.
latinIntro.cn: 意大利语 risco 是目前已知的最早形式。

items.example: Risque carries the word to French.

definition_en: a large natural stream of water, or a large flowing mass
core_image: 顺流漂向远方村庄的小船
scene: 小船顺着河流漂向远处的村庄。The boat drifted down the river toward the far village.
sceneCN: 这里 river 是「河流」（第 1 个义项：天然的大水道）；句意：小船顺着河流漂向远处的村庄。

senses.title: A watercourse
senses.definition: a large natural stream flowing to the sea or a lake
senses.definitionCN: 流向海洋或湖泊的大型天然水道
senses.example: The river flows through three countries.
senses.exampleCN: 这条河流经三个国家。
senses.why: The river is the moving water itself.
senses.whyCN: river 指流动的水本身。

senses.title: A great flow
senses.definition: a large moving mass of people or things
senses.definitionCN: 大量流动的人或物
senses.example: A river of people filled the square.
senses.exampleCN: 人潮如河般填满了广场。
senses.why: Anything flowing in a long line looks like a river.
senses.whyCN: 任何排成长线流动的东西都像一条河。

senses.title: A source of life
senses.definition: the waterway that supports farms, towns and travel
senses.definitionCN: 供养农田、城镇与交通的水道
senses.example: The town grew rich beside the river.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城镇在河边富了起来。
senses.why: Rivers carry water, soil and trade.
senses.whyCN: 河流带来水、泥土与贸易。

intro.en: River comes from Old French riviere, from Latin riparius, of a bank.
intro.cn: river 源自古法语 riviere，来自拉丁语 riparius（河岸的）。

items.en: Ripa means a bank of a stream.
items.cn: ripa 意为溪流的岸。

items.en: Riparius means of a bank.
items.cn: riparius 意为河岸的。

items.en: Riviere shifts from bank to the water itself.
items.cn: riviere 从河岸转为指水本身。

items.en: River enters English as a large stream.
items.cn: river 以大型水道之意进入英语。

items.en: Figurative rivers of people appear.
items.cn: 出现了人潮如河的比喻用法。

note.en: A river is large; a stream or brook is smaller.
note.cn: river 较大，stream 与 brook 较小。

entries.definition: a river or canal used for travel

normalIntro.en: A river is a road made of flowing water.
normalIntro.cn: river 是一条用水流铺成的路。

normal.en: The river bank is the land beside it.
normal.cn: river bank 是河边的陆地。

normal.en: Cross the river means reach the other side.
normal.cn: cross the river 意为到达对岸。

normal.en: Walk along the river for a calm view.
normal.cn: 沿河散步可看到平静的景色。

normal.en: River water is fresh, not salty.
normal.cn: river water 是淡水，不是咸水。

normal.en: An underground river hides below the land.
normal.cn: underground river 藏在地下。

abstract.en: Picture a silver ribbon between green fields.
abstract.cn: 想象绿色田野间一条银色丝带。

abstract.en: Imagine a crowd flowing like water down a street.
abstract.cn: 想象人群像水一样沿街流动。

abstract.en: Think of an old town waking beside the water.
abstract.cn: 想象一座老城在水边苏醒。

examples.en: We swam in the river all afternoon.
examples.cn: 我们整个下午都在河里游泳。

examples.en: The river was too wide to cross.
examples.cn: 河水太宽，过不去。

examples.en: A river of light ran down the hill.
examples.cn: 一道光河沿山坡流下。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「river」听起来像「日我」——每天都流过我身边的水，就是河流。

root: 拉丁语 ripa（河岸）→ riparius（河岸的）→ 古法语 riviere → river，词义由「岸」转指流动的水道。

sensesIntro.en: A river is a large natural waterway, a great flow of people or things, or a lifeline for a place.
sensesIntro.cn: river 指大型天然水道、大量流动的人或物，以及一个地方的生命依托。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a silver ribbon between fields.
core.cn: 核心意象：田野间的银色丝带。

branches.en: The watercourse is the core sense.
branches.cn: 水道是核心义项。

branches.en: Any great flow borrows the image.
branches.cn: 任何大量流动都借用这个意象。

branches.en: Water, soil and trade make a lifeline.
branches.cn: 水、泥土与贸易构成生命线。

branches.en: Water and people both move in long lines.
branches.cn: 水与人都以长线流动。

branches.en: The stream that feeds a town is also its road.
branches.cn: 供养城镇的河流也是它的道路。

intro.en: River descends from Latin ripa, a bank, through French.
intro.cn: river 经由法语源自拉丁语 ripa（河岸）。

latinIntro.en: Ripa and riparius are the Latin steps behind the word.
latinIntro.cn: ripa 与 riparius 是这个词背后的拉丁环节。

items.example: Riviere shifts to the water itself.

items.exampleCN: riverbed 由 river 与 bed 组成。

latinEntries.example: Ripa is the root of river.
latinEntries.exampleCN: ripa 是 river 的词根。

definition_en: a hard way for vehicles, or a route toward a goal
core_image: 雨后泥泞的乡间小路
scene: 雨后乡间的小路泥泞难走，他们放慢了车速。After the rain the country road was muddy, so they drove slowly.
sceneCN: 这里 road 是「道路」（第 1 个义项：供车辆通行的路面）；句意：雨后乡间的小路泥泞难走，他们放慢了车速。

senses.title: A way for vehicles
senses.definition: a hard surface built for cars and other vehicles
senses.definitionCN: 为汽车等车辆修建的坚硬路面
senses.example: The road is closed for repairs.
senses.exampleCN: 这条路因维修封闭。
senses.why: The road is the prepared line of travel.
senses.whyCN: 道路是修整好的通行线路。

senses.title: A journey
senses.definition: travel or a journey along a route
senses.definitionCN: 沿路线行进或旅行
senses.example: The band has been on the road for months.
senses.exampleCN: 乐队已经巡演了好几个月。
senses.why: Being on the road means being in motion.
senses.whyCN: on the road 意为一直在路上。

senses.title: A way to a goal
senses.definition: a course of action leading to a result
senses.definitionCN: 通向结果的行为路径
senses.example: Education is the road to a better life.
senses.exampleCN: 教育是通往更好生活的道路。
senses.why: A goal is reached by following a route.
senses.whyCN: 目标要沿着一条路线才能抵达。

intro.en: Road comes from Old English rād, a riding or journey, from ridan, to ride.
intro.cn: road 源自古英语 rād（骑行、旅程），来自 ridan（骑）。

items.en: Rād means a riding or journey.
items.cn: rād 意为骑行或旅程。

items.en: Road shifts from journey to the way itself.
items.cn: road 由旅程转指道路本身。

items.en: Turnpikes make roads common objects.
items.cn: 收费公路让道路成为常见事物。

items.en: On the road means travelling.
items.cn: on the road 意为在路上旅行。

items.en: Road maps guide both cars and plans.
items.cn: 路线图既指引车辆也指引计划。

note.en: A road is for vehicles; a street usually has buildings beside it.
note.cn: road 供车辆通行，street 通常两侧有建筑。

entries.definition: a road in a town with buildings
the way from one place to another

normalIntro.en: A road began as the act of riding.
normalIntro.cn: road 最初指的是骑行的行为。

normal.en: The main road carries most traffic.
normal.cn: main road 承载大部分车流。

normal.en: Road safety saves lives.
normal.cn: road safety 能拯救生命。

normal.en: On the road means travelling.
normal.cn: on the road 意为在旅途中。

normal.en: A road map shows the way.
normal.cn: road map 显示路线。

normal.en: Cross the road at the lights.
normal.cn: cross the road 要在红绿灯处过。

abstract.en: Picture a wet lane shining after rain.
abstract.cn: 想象雨后发亮的湿漉小路。

abstract.en: Imagine a band's van rolling from town to town.
abstract.cn: 想象乐队的车从小镇开往小镇。

abstract.en: Think of a long straight line toward a bright gate.
abstract.cn: 想象一条通向明亮大门的长直线。

examples.en: The road to the village is very narrow.
examples.cn: 通往村庄的路非常窄。

examples.en: They are on the road again this week.
examples.cn: 他们这周又上路了。

examples.en: Hard work is the road to success.
examples.cn: 努力是通往成功的道路。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「road」听起来像「绕的」——弯来绕去让人走的，就是道路。

root: 古英语 rād（骑行、旅程）→ 行走的路线 → road，核心义「被踩出来、供人前往的路线」。

sensesIntro.en: A road is a way for vehicles, the state of travelling, or a route to a goal.
sensesIntro.cn: road 指车辆通行的道路、在旅途中的状态，或通往目标的途径。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a wet lane shining after rain.
core.cn: 核心意象：雨后发亮的小路。

branches.en: The built way for vehicles is the main sense.
branches.cn: 为车辆修建的路是主要义项。

branches.en: Being on the road is being in motion.
branches.cn: on the road 就是处于行进中。

branches.en: A plan also follows a road to its result.
branches.cn: 计划也沿着一条路抵达结果。

branches.en: The physical way and the journey share one line.
branches.cn: 实体的路与旅程共享同一条线。

branches.en: Travelling and striving both mean moving toward something.
branches.cn: 旅行与奋斗都意味着朝某处前进。

intro.en: Road comes from Old English rād, riding or journey.
intro.cn: road 源自古英语 rād（骑行、旅程）。

latinIntro.en: The word is Germanic and shares a root with ride.
latinIntro.cn: 该词属于日耳曼语，与 ride 同源。

items.example: Road shifted to the way itself.

items.exampleCN: roadblock 由 road 与 block 组成。

items.meaning: map of roads or a plan
items.exampleCN: road map 延伸到计划含义。

definition_en: a large stone, to move gently back and forth, or rock music
core_image: 海浪拍打的岸边岩石
scene: 海浪不断拍打着岸边的岩石。Waves kept beating against the rocks on the shore.
sceneCN: 这里 rock 是「岩石」（第 1 个义项：大块坚硬的石头）；句意：海浪不断拍打着岸边的岩石。

senses.title: A large stone
senses.definition: a large hard mass of stone
senses.definitionCN: 大块坚硬的石头
senses.example: A grey rock stood at the path's end.
senses.exampleCN: 小路尽头立着一块灰色岩石。
senses.why: The solid stone is the oldest sense.
senses.whyCN: 坚实的石头是最古老的义项。

senses.title: Moving gently
senses.definition: to move gently from side to side
senses.definitionCN: 轻轻地左右移动
senses.example: She rocked the child to sleep.
senses.exampleCN: 她轻摇孩子入睡。
senses.why: The cradle repeats a slow side-to-side motion.
senses.whyCN: 摇篮重复着缓慢的左右摆动。

senses.title: Rock music
senses.definition: a loud popular music with strong beat
senses.definitionCN: 节奏强劲的响亮流行音乐
senses.example: The band plays old rock.
senses.exampleCN: 这支乐队演奏老摇滚。
senses.why: The music took the name of its rolling beat.
senses.whyCN: 这种音乐沿用了它翻滚般节奏的名字。

intro.en: Rock comes from Old French roche, from Medieval Latin rocca, a crag.
intro.cn: rock 源自古法语 roche，来自中世纪拉丁语 rocca（岩崖）。

items.en: Rocca means a crag or rock.
items.cn: rocca 意为岩崖或岩石。

items.en: Old French roche carries the stone sense.
items.cn: 古法语 roche 保留石头义。

items.en: Rock names stone, then a gentle sway.
items.cn: rock 先指石头，后指轻摇。

items.en: Rock music rises in the mid twentieth century.
items.cn: 摇滚乐在二十世纪中叶兴起。

items.en: Rock and roll links the sway and the sound.
items.cn: rock and roll 把摇摆与声音联系起来。

note.en: A rock is big and solid; a stone is smaller.
note.cn: rock 是大而坚实的石块，stone 通常更小。

entries.definition: a rocking chair or rock musician
to move slowly side to side

normalIntro.en: Rock is stone, a sway, and a rolling beat.
normalIntro.cn: rock 既是石头，也是摇摆，还是一种翻滚的节奏。

normal.en: A large rock blocks the narrow path.
normal.cn: a large rock 堵住了狭窄的小路。

normal.en: Rock the baby gently in your arms.
normal.cn: rock the baby 就是在怀里轻轻摇晃婴儿。

normal.en: Rock climbing needs strong hands.
normal.cn: rock climbing 需要有力的双手。

normal.en: Solid rock is hard to dig through.
normal.cn: solid rock 很难挖穿。

normal.en: Rock music has a strong beat.
normal.cn: rock music 节奏强劲。

abstract.en: Picture waves striking a grey shore rock.
abstract.cn: 想象海浪拍打灰色的岸边岩石。

abstract.en: Imagine a cradle swinging in a quiet room.
abstract.cn: 想象安静房间里摆动的摇篮。

abstract.en: Think of a stage shaking with a heavy beat.
abstract.cn: 想象舞台随沉重节拍震动。

examples.en: The boat hit a rock near the shore.
examples.cn: 小船在岸边撞上了岩石。

examples.en: He rocked the chair back and forth.
examples.cn: 他让椅子前后摇晃。

examples.en: They listened to rock all night.
examples.cn: 他们整夜听摇滚乐。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「rock」听起来像「落磕」——从山上落下来磕人的硬块，就是岩石。

root: 中世纪拉丁语 rocca（岩崖）→ 古法语 roche → rock，核心义「坚硬的大石」，再由摇篮的摆动引申出摇动与摇滚乐。

sensesIntro.en: Rock means a large stone, a gentle swaying motion, or rock music.
sensesIntro.cn: rock 意为大块岩石、轻轻摇动，或摇滚乐。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a grey stone in moving waves.
core.cn: 核心意象：波浪中的灰色岩石。

branches.en: The stone is the oldest noun sense.
branches.cn: 石头是最古老的名词义项。

branches.en: The gentle sway is the verb sense.
branches.cn: 轻摇是动词义项。

branches.en: Rock music takes the rolling beat.
branches.cn: 摇滚乐沿用了翻滚的节拍。

branches.en: Even a heavy rock can rock in an earthquake.
branches.cn: 连沉重的岩石也会在地震中摇晃。

branches.en: The cradle sway and the music beat share motion.
branches.cn: 摇篮摆动与音乐节拍都共享运动感。

intro.en: Rock descends from Old French roche, a crag.
intro.cn: rock 源自古法语 roche（岩崖）。

latinIntro.en: Medieval Latin rocca is the earliest known form.
latinIntro.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 rocca 是目前已知最早的形式。

items.example: Rocker names a chair or player.
The phrase joins sway and music.
items.exampleCN: 这个短语把摇摆与音乐连在一起。

latinEntries.example: Rocca is the source of rock.
latinEntries.exampleCN: rocca 是 rock 的来源。

definition_en: the part an actor plays, or the function a person or thing has in a situation
core_image: 一卷写着台词的纸
scene: 她在剧中扮演一位年轻的医生。She played the role of a young doctor in the play.
sceneCN: 这里 role 是「角色」（第 1 个义项）；句意：她在剧中扮演一位年轻的医生。

senses.title: Actor's part
senses.definition: the character that an actor plays in a film or play
senses.definitionCN: 演员在电影或戏剧中扮演的人物
senses.example: He won an award for his role in the film.
senses.exampleCN: 他因在这部电影中的角色获奖。
senses.why: The actor takes up one written part.
senses.whyCN: 演员承担起一份写好的台词。

senses.title: Function
senses.definition: the purpose or effect that someone or something has
senses.definitionCN: 某人或某物所具有的用途或影响
senses.example: Salt plays a key role in the recipe.
senses.exampleCN: 盐在这道食谱中起关键作用。
senses.why: The part idea moves from stage to real life.
senses.whyCN: 「角色」这一概念从舞台走进现实。

senses.title: Duty
senses.definition: the expected duty or position of a person in a group
senses.definitionCN: 一个人在群体中被期待的职责或位置
senses.example: Her role is to train the new staff.
senses.exampleCN: 她的职责是培训新员工。
senses.why: A part in the group comes with duties.
senses.whyCN: 在群体中的位置伴随职责。

intro.en: Role comes from French rôle, a roll of paper with an actor's lines.
intro.cn: role 源自法语 rôle，指写着演员台词的纸卷。

items.en: Rotulus means a little roll of paper.
items.cn: rotulus 意为小纸卷。

items.en: Rotulus also gives the word roll.
items.cn: rotulus 也给出 roll 这个词。

items.en: Rôle is the roll holding an actor's lines.
items.cn: rôle 是写有演员台词的纸卷。

items.en: English role moves from the scroll to the part played.
items.cn: 英语 role 从纸卷转指所演的角色。

items.en: Role also means a function in a group.
items.cn: role 又指在群体中的作用。

note.en: A role is a part; a roll is a rolled object.
note.cn: role 是角色，roll 则是卷起的东西。

entries.definition: a statement about what is allowed

normalIntro.en: A role is a part you take on stage or in life.
normalIntro.cn: role 是你在舞台上或生活中承担的角色。

normal.en: She has the leading role in the play.
normal.cn: 她在这部戏里演主角。

normal.en: Water plays a key role in growth.
normal.cn: 水在生长中起关键作用。

normal.en: A teacher can be a role model.
normal.cn: 老师可以成为榜样。

normal.en: His role is to guard the gate.
normal.cn: 他的职责是守门。

normal.en: The role of the press is to inform.
normal.cn: 新闻界的作用是传递信息。

abstract.en: Picture a rolled script with one part marked.
abstract.cn: 想象一卷剧本，其中一段被标出。

abstract.en: Imagine a mask that shows who you are today.
abstract.cn: 想象一张显示你今天身份的面具。

abstract.en: Think of a seat reserved for one person in a team.
abstract.cn: 想象团队中为某人保留的座位。

examples.en: The role requires a strong singing voice.
examples.cn: 这个角色需要一副好嗓子。

examples.en: Parents play an important role in education.
examples.cn: 父母在教育中起重要作用。

examples.en: Each member has a clear role in the project.
examples.cn: 每个成员在项目中都有明确职责。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「role」和「roll」同音——演员拿到的那卷纸，就是他要在台上扮演的角色。

root: 法语 rôle（台词纸卷）来自拉丁语 rotulus（小卷）→ role，核心义「分配给一个人的那一份」。

sensesIntro.en: Role means a character in a play, or a function and duty in real life.
sensesIntro.cn: role 意为戏剧角色，或现实中的作用与职责。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a rolled paper with lines for one actor.
core.cn: 核心意象：写着一位演员台词的纸卷。

branches.en: The actor's part is the first sense.
branches.cn: 演员的角色是第一个义项。

branches.en: The part becomes a function in life.
branches.cn: 角色变成现实中的功能。

branches.en: A position in a group brings duties.
branches.cn: 群体中的位置带来职责。

branches.en: Both are parts played within a whole.
branches.cn: 两者都是整体中被承担的一份。

branches.en: Function and duty both define a place.
branches.cn: 作用与职责都界定了位置。

intro.en: Role goes back through French to Latin rotulus, a little roll.
intro.cn: role 经法语追溯到拉丁语 rotulus，意为小卷。

latinIntro.en: Rotulus gives French rôle and English role.
latinIntro.cn: rotulus 给出法语 rôle 与英语 role。

items.example: Play a role is a common phrase.
items.exampleCN: play a role 是常用短语。
roleplay 由 role 与 play 组合。

items.example: Role model means a person to copy.
items.exampleCN: role model 意为可供效仿的人。

latinEntries.example: Rotulus is the source of role.
latinEntries.exampleCN: rotulus 是 role 的来源。

definition_zh: 滚动；卷起；转动；面包卷；名单
definition_en: to move by turning over and over, to wrap something around itself, or a small round loaf
core_image: 一只沿着斜坡滚下的圆罐
scene: 那个空罐子沿着人行道滚了下去。The empty can rolled down the sidewalk.
sceneCN: 这里 roll 是「滚动」（第 1 个义项）；句意：那个空罐子沿着人行道滚了下去。

senses.title: Turn over
senses.definition: to move forward by turning over and over
senses.definitionCN: 通过不断翻转而向前移动
senses.example: The ball rolled across the floor.
senses.exampleCN: 球滚过地板。
senses.why: A round object keeps turning as it goes.
senses.whyCN: 圆形物体一边前进一边不停翻转。

senses.title: Wrap around
senses.definition: to wrap something around itself or around another thing
senses.definitionCN: 把某物卷起来或缠绕在别物上
senses.example: She rolled the map into a tube.
senses.exampleCN: 她把地图卷成了一个筒。
senses.why: The flat thing is turned around itself.
senses.whyCN: 平的东西绕着自身转起来。

senses.title: Bread and list
senses.definition: a small round loaf, or an official list of names
senses.definitionCN: 小圆面包，或正式的人名名单
senses.example: The clerk read the roll of new members.
senses.exampleCN: 职员念了新成员名单。
senses.why: A rolled shape names bread; a rolled sheet names a list.
senses.whyCN: 卷起的形状命名面包，卷起的纸页命名名单。

intro.en: Roll comes from Latin rotula, a small wheel.
intro.cn: roll 源自拉丁语 rotula，意为小轮子。

items.en: Rotula means a small wheel.
items.cn: rotula 意为小轮。

items.en: Rotare means to turn like a wheel.
items.cn: rotare 意为像轮子一样转。

items.en: Old French rolle names a rolled document.
items.cn: 古法语 rolle 指卷起的文书。

items.en: English roll covers turning and wrapping.
items.cn: 英语 roll 涵盖滚动与卷起。

items.en: Roll also names bread and a name list.
items.cn: roll 又指面包卷与人名名单。

note.en: Roll is the action; role is the part played.
note.cn: roll 是滚动的动作，role 则是扮演的角色。

entries.definition: a part played by an actor
to fish by pulling a line

normalIntro.en: Roll turns round and round, and also wraps things up.
normalIntro.cn: roll 一圈圈地转，也把东西卷起来。

normal.en: The barrel rolled down the hill.
normal.cn: 木桶滚下山坡。

normal.en: Please roll the paper into a tube.
normal.cn: 请把纸卷成筒。

normal.en: He rolled up his sleeves and worked.
normal.cn: 他卷起袖子干活。

normal.en: The bakery sells warm rolls at noon.
normal.cn: 面包店中午卖热乎的面包卷。

normal.en: The teacher called the roll at nine.
normal.cn: 老师九点点名。

abstract.en: Picture a round can gaining speed downhill.
abstract.cn: 想象一个圆罐在斜坡上越滚越快。

abstract.en: Imagine a sheet curling into a tight tube.
abstract.cn: 想象一张纸卷成紧实的筒。

abstract.en: Think of a warm bread roll on a plate.
abstract.cn: 想象盘子里一只热面包卷。

examples.en: The coin rolled under the table.
examples.cn: 硬币滚到了桌子下面。

examples.en: They rolled the carpet before moving it.
examples.cn: 他们搬地毯前把它卷了起来。

examples.en: A fresh roll came with the soup.
examples.cn: 汤配了一只新鲜面包卷。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「roll」读起来像轮子转的「隆隆」声——圆的东西一直转就是滚动，把纸一直转就是卷起。

root: 拉丁语 rotula（小轮）与 rotare（转动）→ 古法语 rolle → roll，核心义「绕着自身转」。

sensesIntro.en: Roll means to move by turning, to wrap into a tube, or a bread roll and name list.
sensesIntro.cn: roll 意为翻转滚动、卷成筒状，或指面包卷与名单。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a round can rolling downhill.
core.cn: 核心意象：沿坡滚下的圆罐。

branches.en: Turning movement is the core sense.
branches.cn: 翻转移动是核心义项。

branches.en: Wrapping is turning a flat thing around itself.
branches.cn: 卷起是让平面绕自身转。

branches.en: Rolled shapes name both bread and lists.
branches.cn: 卷起的形状既命名面包也命名名单。

branches.en: Both senses depend on rotation.
branches.cn: 两者都依赖旋转。

branches.en: The rolled form links the noun senses.
branches.cn: 卷起的形态连接了名词义项。

intro.en: Roll comes from Latin rotula through French rolle.
intro.cn: roll 经法语 rolle 来自拉丁语 rotula。

latinIntro.en: Rotula and rotare give the turning image.
latinIntro.cn: rotula 与 rotare 提供旋转的意象。

items.exampleCN: rolling 加上了表示活动的词尾。

latinEntries.example: Rotula is the source of roll.
latinEntries.exampleCN: rotula 是 roll 的来源。

definition_en: the covering on top of a building or vehicle, or to put a cover on top
core_image: 雨中的一片斜屋顶
scene: 雨水从老房子的屋顶漏进屋里。Rain leaked through the roof of the old house.
sceneCN: 这里 roof 是「屋顶」（第 1 个义项）；句意：雨水从老房子的屋顶漏进屋里。

senses.title: Building top
senses.definition: the structure that covers the top of a building
senses.definitionCN: 覆盖在建筑物顶部的结构
senses.example: The wind tore tiles from the roof.
senses.exampleCN: 大风把瓦片从屋顶上刮了下来。
senses.why: The cover closes the house from above.
senses.whyCN: 这层覆盖物从上方把房子盖住。

senses.title: Vehicle top
senses.definition: the top part of a car or other vehicle
senses.definitionCN: 汽车或其他交通工具的顶部
senses.example: They tied the bikes to the roof of the car.
senses.exampleCN: 他们把自行车绑在车顶上。
senses.why: The same covering idea moves to a vehicle.
senses.whyCN: 同样的覆盖概念被移用到车辆上。

senses.title: To cover
senses.definition: to put a roof or cover on a building
senses.definitionCN: 给建筑物加盖屋顶或覆盖物
senses.example: Workers roofed the barn before winter.
senses.exampleCN: 工人在入冬前给谷仓盖好了顶。
senses.why: The noun turns into the act of covering.
senses.whyCN: 名词转成覆盖这一动作。

intro.en: Roof comes from Old English hrof, the cover of a house.
intro.cn: roof 源自古代英语 hrof，意为房屋的覆盖物。

items.en: Hrof names the cover over a building.
items.cn: hrof 指建筑物上方的覆盖物。

items.en: Hrof keeps the same meaning in the north.
items.cn: hrof 在北方语言中保持相同含义。

items.en: Rof settles into the modern spelling.
items.cn: rof 逐渐过渡到现代拼写。

items.en: Roof extends from houses to cars and buses.
items.cn: roof 从房屋扩展到汽车和巴士。

items.en: Roof garden adds the idea of use on top.
items.cn: roof garden 增加了在顶上使用的含义。

note.en: A roof covers a building; a ceiling covers a room.
note.cn: roof 覆盖整栋建筑，ceiling 则覆盖房间内部。

entries.definition: the hard foot of a horse
the top surface of a roof
the inside top of a room

normalIntro.en: A roof is the cover that sits on top.
normalIntro.cn: roof 是盖在顶上的那层覆盖物。

normal.en: Snow lay thick on the roof.
normal.cn: 屋顶上积了厚厚的雪。

normal.en: They built a roof garden on the flat top.
normal.cn: 他们在平顶上建了屋顶花园。

normal.en: The roof rack holds two bicycles.
normal.cn: 车顶架放着两辆自行车。

normal.en: The whole family lives under one roof.
normal.cn: 一家人住在同一屋檐下。

normal.en: The crowd raised the roof at the concert.
normal.cn: 音乐会上人群喧闹欢腾。

abstract.en: Picture a steep roof shining after rain.
abstract.cn: 想象雨后发亮的陡斜屋顶。

abstract.en: Imagine a hand pulling a cover over a box.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手把盖子拉到箱子上。

abstract.en: Think of one wide roof sheltering many people.
abstract.cn: 想象一片宽大的屋顶庇护着许多人。

examples.en: A bird built its nest under the roof.
examples.cn: 一只鸟在屋檐下筑巢。

examples.en: The sun beat down on the car roof.
examples.cn: 烈日晒在车顶上。

examples.en: They roofed the shed with cheap boards.
examples.cn: 他们用便宜木板给棚子盖了顶。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「roof」像「如夫」——像丈夫一样撑在头顶上遮风挡雨的那一层，就是屋顶。

root: 古代英语 hrof（房屋覆盖物）与古诺斯语同源，核心义「盖在顶上的保护层」。

sensesIntro.en: Roof means the cover of a building, the top of a vehicle, or to put such a cover on.
sensesIntro.cn: roof 意为建筑物屋顶、车辆顶部，或给某物加盖顶。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sloped roof in the rain.
core.cn: 核心意象：雨中的斜屋顶。

branches.en: The building cover is the main sense.
branches.cn: 建筑屋顶是主要义项。

branches.en: The vehicle top borrows the same cover.
branches.cn: 车辆顶部借用同样的覆盖概念。

branches.en: The verb names putting the cover on.
branches.cn: 动词指加上覆盖物。

branches.en: Building and covering share one structure.
branches.cn: 建筑与盖顶共享同一结构。

branches.en: Both protect what lies beneath.
branches.cn: 两者都保护下方之物。

intro.en: Roof is an old Germanic word with English compounds.
intro.cn: roof 是古老的日耳曼词，并有许多英语复合词。

latinIntro.en: Roof has no Latin root; English builds new words from it.
latinIntro.cn: roof 没有拉丁词根，英语在它之上构成新词。

definition_en: a part of a building with walls, or the space needed for something
core_image: 一间空荡的房间
scene: 屋里已经放不下一张更大的桌子了。There is no room for a larger table in here.
sceneCN: 这里 room 是「空间」（第 2 个义项）；句意：屋里已经放不下一张更大的桌子了。

senses.title: Walled space
senses.definition: a part of a building with walls, a floor, and a ceiling
senses.definitionCN: 建筑物中用墙、地板和天花板隔出的一部分
senses.example: The dining room faces the garden.
senses.exampleCN: 餐厅朝向花园。
senses.why: Walls make a separate space inside a house.
senses.whyCN: 墙壁在房子里隔出一块独立空间。

senses.title: Space
senses.definition: the empty space that is available for people or things
senses.definitionCN: 可供人或物使用的空余空间
senses.example: There is little room left in the car.
senses.exampleCN: 车里剩下的空间不多了。
senses.why: The empty area is the same idea without walls.
senses.whyCN: 空出来的区域就是没有墙的空间概念。

senses.title: Scope
senses.definition: the chance or scope for something to happen or improve
senses.definitionCN: 某事发生或改进的机会与余地
senses.example: The plan leaves room for change.
senses.exampleCN: 这个计划留有改动的余地。
senses.why: Free space becomes free possibility.
senses.whyCN: 空余空间转成空余可能性。

intro.en: Room comes from Old English rum, meaning spacious.
intro.cn: room 源自古代英语 rum，意为宽敞的。

items.en: Rum means space or a spacious place.
items.cn: rum 意为空间或宽敞之处。

items.en: Rum also describes something wide and open.
items.cn: rum 也形容宽大开阔之物。

items.en: Roum narrows to a part of a house.
items.cn: roum 收窄为房屋中的一个部分。

items.en: Room keeps both the walled and open senses.
items.cn: room 同时保留有墙房间与开放空间两义。

items.en: Room for improvement becomes a common phrase.
items.cn: room for improvement 成为常用短语。

note.en: A room has walls; space is open area.
note.cn: room 通常指有墙的房间，space 则是开放的空间。

entries.definition: the part of a plant underground

normalIntro.en: A room is space you can walk into or use.
normalIntro.cn: room 是你可以走进去或使用的空间。

normal.en: The living room opens onto a small balcony.
normal.cn: 客厅通向一个小阳台。

normal.en: Please make room for the new books.
normal.cn: 请为新书腾出空间。

normal.en: Room service brought breakfast at seven.
normal.cn: 客房服务七点送来了早餐。

normal.en: There is room for improvement in the essay.
normal.cn: 这篇文章还有改进余地。

normal.en: We booked a double room for two nights.
normal.cn: 我们订了两晚的双人房。

abstract.en: Picture a bare room with sunlight on the floor.
abstract.cn: 想象一间空房间，阳光落在地板上。

abstract.en: Imagine an empty shelf with space to spare.
abstract.cn: 想象一个还留有空位的架子。

abstract.en: Think of an open door leading to a wider place.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇通向更宽敞之处的门。

examples.en: The room was quiet and full of light.
examples.cn: 房间安静而明亮。

examples.en: We need more room for the guests.
examples.cn: 我们需要更多空间招待客人。

examples.en: There is still room to improve the design.
examples.cn: 这个设计仍有改进余地。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「room」读音像「如木」——木头隔出的空处就是房间；空着的部分就是空间与余地。

root: 古代英语 rum（宽敞、空间）→ room，核心义「空出来的地方」。

sensesIntro.en: Room means a walled part of a building, available space, or scope for something.
sensesIntro.cn: room 意为有墙的房间、可用空间，或做某事的余地。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an empty room with light on the floor.
core.cn: 核心意象：阳光落在地板上的空房间。

branches.en: The walled area is the first sense.
branches.cn: 有墙的空间是第一个义项。

branches.en: Open space needs no walls.
branches.cn: 开放空间并不需要墙。

branches.en: Free space becomes free possibility.
branches.cn: 空余空间变成空余可能。

branches.en: Both senses are measured in area.
branches.cn: 两者都以面积衡量。

branches.en: Spare room allows things to change.
branches.cn: 留有余地才能发生变化。

intro.en: Room is an old English word that builds compounds.
intro.cn: room 是古老的英语词，并构成许多复合词。

latinIntro.en: Room has no Latin root; its family is English and Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: room 没有拉丁词根，它的词族属于英语与日耳曼语。

items.example: Rum gives the idea of open space.
items.exampleCN: rum 给出开放空间的概念。
roommate 由 room 与 mate 组合。

items.meaning: all the people a room holds
items.exampleCN: roomful 加上了表数量的词尾。

definition_en: a strong thick cord, the skills needed for a job, or to tie something with a rope
core_image: 盘在甲板上的粗绳
scene: 登山者把绳子牢牢系在岩石上。The climber tied the rope firmly to the rock.
sceneCN: 这里 rope 是「绳索」（第 1 个义项）；句意：登山者把绳子牢牢系在岩石上。

senses.title: Strong cord
senses.definition: a strong thick cord made of twisted threads
senses.definitionCN: 由多股线拧成的结实粗绳
senses.example: The boat was tied with a thick rope.
senses.exampleCN: 船用一根粗绳系住了。
senses.why: Twisted threads make one strong line.
senses.whyCN: 拧在一起的线形成一根结实的绳。

senses.title: Know-how
senses.definition: the skills and knowledge needed for a job
senses.definitionCN: 从事某项工作所需的技能与知识
senses.example: It took a month to learn the ropes.
senses.exampleCN: 熟悉门道花了一个月。
senses.why: A sailor must know every rope on the ship.
senses.whyCN: 水手必须认识船上的每一根绳。

senses.title: Tie or fence
senses.definition: to tie something with a rope or keep people back with one
senses.definitionCN: 用绳子捆住某物，或用绳子把人隔开
senses.example: Police roped off the narrow lane.
senses.exampleCN: 警察用绳子把窄巷隔开。
senses.why: The noun becomes the act of using the cord.
senses.whyCN: 名词转成使用绳索的动作。

intro.en: Rope comes from Old English rap, a strong cord.
intro.cn: rope 源自古代英语 rap，意为结实的绳。

items.en: Rap names a strong twisted cord.
items.cn: rap 指结实的拧绳。

items.en: Related forms name a cord in other northern tongues.
items.cn: 其他北方语言中的相关形式也指绳索。

items.en: Rope becomes the standard spelling.
items.cn: rope 成为标准拼写。

items.en: Sailors learn the ropes of a ship.
items.cn: 水手要熟悉船上的绳索。

items.en: Learn the ropes comes to mean know-how.
items.cn: learn the ropes 转指掌握门道。

note.en: A rope is thick; a robe is clothing.
note.cn: rope 是粗绳，robe 则是长袍。

entries.definition: a wish for a good result
a thick strong wire or rope

normalIntro.en: Rope ties things, and knowing your ropes means knowing the job.
normalIntro.cn: rope 把东西系住，熟悉绳索则意味着熟悉工作。

normal.en: He tied the boat with a heavy rope.
normal.cn: 他用一根粗绳把船系好。

normal.en: The children played with a jump rope.
normal.cn: 孩子们玩跳绳。

normal.en: They climbed down a rope ladder.
normal.cn: 他们顺着绳梯爬下去。

normal.en: Workers roped off the wet floor.
normal.cn: 工人用绳子把湿滑地面隔开。

normal.en: It takes time to learn the ropes.
normal.cn: 熟悉门道需要时间。

abstract.en: Picture a coil of rope on a wooden deck.
abstract.cn: 想象木甲板上盘着的一卷绳。

abstract.en: Imagine many threads twisting into one strong line.
abstract.cn: 想象许多细线拧成一根结实的绳。

abstract.en: Think of a rope barrier holding a crowd back.
abstract.cn: 想象一道绳栏把人群挡在后面。

examples.en: The rescue team threw a rope to the swimmer.
examples.cn: 救援队把绳子抛给游泳者。

examples.en: She learned the ropes of the new job quickly.
examples.cn: 她很快熟悉了新工作的门道。

examples.en: The garden was roped off for repairs.
examples.cn: 花园因维修被绳子围了起来。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「rope」像「绕」——许多细线绕在一起，就成了结实的绳索。

root: 古代英语 rap（结实的绳索），核心义「多股拧成、用于系绑的长索」。

sensesIntro.en: Rope means a strong thick cord, the know-how for a job, or to tie or fence with a cord.
sensesIntro.cn: rope 意为结实粗绳、工作中的门道，或用绳捆扎与围隔。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a coil of rope on a deck.
core.cn: 核心意象：甲板上盘着的一卷绳。

branches.en: The strong cord is the main sense.
branches.cn: 结实绳索是主要义项。

branches.en: Knowing the ropes means knowing the job.
branches.cn: 熟悉绳索就是熟悉工作。

branches.en: The verb puts the cord to use.
branches.cn: 动词把绳索用于行动。

branches.en: Cord and tying belong together.
branches.cn: 绳索与系绑密不可分。

branches.en: The sailor image links tool and skill.
branches.cn: 水手形象连接了工具与技能。

intro.en: Rope is an Old English word with a small English family.
intro.cn: rope 是古代英语词，有一个小小的英语词族。

latinIntro.en: Rope has no Latin root; its history is Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: rope 没有拉丁词根，其历史属于日耳曼语。

definition_zh: 圆的；围绕；一轮；一回合；绕行
definition_en: shaped like a circle, surrounding something, or one stage in a series
core_image: 一张围坐的圆桌
scene: 客人围坐在桌旁。The guests sat round the table.
sceneCN: 这里 round 是「围绕」（第 2 个义项）；句意：客人围坐在桌旁。

senses.title: Circle shape
senses.definition: shaped like a circle or a ball
senses.definitionCN: 形状像圆圈或球体
senses.example: They sat at a round table.
senses.exampleCN: 他们坐在一张圆桌旁。
senses.why: The shape has no corners and curves all the way.
senses.whyCN: 这个形状没有角，一路弯曲。

senses.title: Surrounding
senses.definition: on every side of something, or moving in a circle
senses.definitionCN: 在某物的各侧，或沿圆圈移动
senses.example: We walked round the old city wall.
senses.exampleCN: 我们绕着古城墙走了一圈。
senses.why: The circle shape becomes a path around a thing.
senses.whyCN: 圆形变成围绕某物的一条路径。

senses.title: One stage
senses.definition: one stage in a competition or a series of events
senses.definitionCN: 比赛或一系列事件中的一个阶段
senses.example: The team won in the first round.
senses.exampleCN: 这支队伍在第一轮获胜。
senses.why: Events complete a circle and start again.
senses.whyCN: 事件走完一圈又重新开始。

senses.title: Go around
senses.definition: to move around something or turn a corner
senses.definitionCN: 绕过某物或转过拐角
senses.example: The bus rounded the corner slowly.
senses.exampleCN: 公交车慢慢转过拐角。
senses.why: The verb turns the circle into movement.
senses.whyCN: 动词把圆圈变成移动。

intro.en: Round comes from Latin rotundus, round, through French rond.
intro.cn: round 经法语 rond 源自拉丁语 rotundus，意为圆的。

items.en: Rotundus means round or wheel-like.
items.cn: rotundus 意为圆的、像轮子的。

items.en: Rota means wheel.
items.cn: rota 意为车轮。

items.en: Old French rond keeps the circular sense.
items.cn: 古法语 rond 保留圆形含义。

items.en: English round covers shape, path, and stage.
items.cn: 英语 round 涵盖形状、路径与阶段。

items.en: Round trip and round table become common phrases.
items.cn: round trip 与 round table 成为常用短语。

note.en: Round is the shape; around is the position.
note.cn: round 多指形状，around 多指位置。

normalIntro.en: Round shapes make paths, turns, and stages.
normalIntro.cn: 圆的形状衍生出路径、转弯与轮次。

normal.en: They bought a round table for the kitchen.
normal.cn: 他们为厨房买了一张圆桌。

normal.en: The moon is round tonight.
normal.cn: 今晚的月亮是圆的。

normal.en: The children ran round the garden.
normal.cn: 孩子们绕着花园跑。

normal.en: She passed the first round easily.
normal.cn: 她轻松通过了第一轮。

normal.en: The car rounded the bend at speed.
normal.cn: 汽车高速转过弯道。

abstract.en: Picture a round table with chairs all around.
abstract.cn: 想象一张四周摆满椅子的圆桌。

abstract.en: Imagine a path circling a small garden.
abstract.cn: 想象一条绕着花园的小路。

abstract.en: Think of a clock hand sweeping in a circle.
abstract.cn: 想象钟表指针画出一圈。

examples.en: The pond is perfectly round.
examples.cn: 这个池塘圆得很规整。

examples.en: We traveled round the island by bus.
examples.cn: 我们乘巴士环岛旅行。

examples.en: The final round starts at noon.
examples.cn: 决赛轮中午开始。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「round」像「绕」——绕成一圈就是圆的；沿着圈走就是围绕；走完一圈就是一轮。

root: 拉丁语 rotundus（圆的）与 rota（轮）→ 法语 rond → round，核心义「绕成一圈的形状与路径」。

sensesIntro.en: Round means circular, surrounding, one stage in a series, or to go around.
sensesIntro.cn: round 意为圆形的、围绕的、一轮一回合，或绕行。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a round table with chairs around it.
core.cn: 核心意象：四周摆着椅子的圆桌。

branches.en: The circular shape is the first sense.
branches.cn: 圆形是第一个义项。

branches.en: The circle becomes a path around things.
branches.cn: 圆圈变成绕行路径。

branches.en: A full circle of events is one round.
branches.cn: 事件走完一圈就是一轮。

branches.en: The verb turns the shape into motion.
branches.cn: 动词把形状变成运动。

branches.en: Both follow a circular order.
branches.cn: 两者都遵循循环顺序。

intro.en: Round comes from Latin rotundus and French rond.
intro.cn: round 来自拉丁语 rotundus 与法语 rond。

latinIntro.en: Rota and rotundus supply the wheel image.
latinIntro.cn: rota 与 rotundus 提供车轮意象。

items.exampleCN: roundabout 由 round 与 about 组合。

latinEntries.example: Rotundus is the source of round.
latinEntries.exampleCN: rotundus 是 round 的来源。

definition_zh: 一排；一列；划船；连续的一段时间；（口语）争吵
definition_en: a line of things or people, to move a boat with oars, a period of continuous success, or a noisy quarrel
core_image: 一串首尾相连的东西：椅子排成行，船桨把水面划出一道直线
scene: 教室里椅子排得整整齐齐。The students sat quietly in the first row of the classroom.
sceneCN: 这里 row 是「一排；一列」（第 1 个义项：横向排成的一行）；句意：学生们安静地坐在教室的第一排。

pos.zh: 一排；一列；划船；（口语）争吵

derivatives.zh: 由动词加 -er 后缀构成，义为「划船者；划艇选手」
由现在分词转名词，义为「划船运动」

senses.title: A line of things
senses.definition: a straight line of people or things side by side
senses.definitionCN: 人或物肩并肩排成的一条直线
senses.example: There is a row of shops near my home.
senses.exampleCN: 我家附近有一排商店。
senses.why: Things placed one after another along a line form the basic picture.
senses.whyCN: 东西沿一条线首尾相接地摆放，构成了这个词最基本的画面。

senses.title: To move a boat with oars
senses.definition: to make a boat move forward using oars
senses.definitionCN: 用桨使船前进
senses.example: We rowed across the lake.
senses.exampleCN: 我们划船穿过湖面。
senses.why: Oars pull the water in long straight lines, like a row of strokes.
senses.whyCN: 船桨在水面拉出一道道长直线，与「一排」的线性意象相通，故借指划船。

senses.title: Continuous success
senses.definition: a period of repeated wins or events, used in phrases like in a row
senses.definitionCN: 接连发生的胜负或事件，用于 in a row 等短语
senses.example: Our team has won five games in a row.
senses.exampleCN: 我们队已经连赢五场。
senses.why: Successes lined up one after another are like objects placed in a row.
senses.whyCN: 接连的胜利像排成一行的物体，一个紧接一个，故由排列义引申出连续义。

senses.title: A noisy quarrel
senses.definition: a loud argument between people, informal British English
senses.definitionCN: 人与人之间的大声争执，英式英语口语
senses.example: They had a row about the money.
senses.exampleCN: 他们为了钱吵了一架。
senses.why: This sense is generally considered a separate word of unknown origin that merged in sound with the line word.
senses.whyCN: 一般认为这是一个来源不确定的同音异源词，因读音相同而在书写上与「一排」混同。

intro.en: Row as a line comes from Old English rāw, while row as an argument is a separate word of uncertain origin.
intro.cn: row 的「一排」义源自古英语 rāw；「争吵」义则是一个来源不确定的同音异源词。

items.en: A Germanic root related to straight lines is reconstructed for the line sense.
items.cn: 「一排」义一般认为可重构出与「直线排列」相关的日耳曼语词根。

items.en: Rāw means a line or row of things.
items.cn: 古英语 rāw 意为一行、一列，指事物排成的直线。

items.en: Row keeps the line sense; the boat sense grows from pulling oars in lines.
items.cn: 中古英语 row 保留排列义；划船义由船桨成排划水的动作发展而来。

items.en: The quarrel sense first appears in the eighteenth century with no secure etymology.
items.cn: 「争吵」义首见于十八世纪，词源无定论，多认为是另一个词的同音混同。

items.en: In a row for continuous wins becomes a fixed phrase.
items.cn: 现代英语中 in a row 固定为表示「连续」的短语，广泛用于比分与纪录。

note.en: Row has a sound-alike verb and near-meaning words about lines and boats.
note.cn: row 有一个同音异源的近形词，近义词集中在排列与划船两个义场。

entries.definition: a cooked mixture of flour and fat for sauces
entries.definitionCN: （烹饪用的）油面酱，拼写相近但词源是法语，与 row 无关，只是形近
生的；未煮过的，字母顺序颠倒后读音相近，词源不同

entries.definition: to make a loud deep sound
entries.definitionCN: 吼叫；轰鸣，与 row 拼写只差一个字母，但属拟声词，来源不同

entries.definition: a row of people or things
entries.definitionCN: 排；行列，泛指一切排成的直线，与 row 的排列义基本重合

entries.definition: to move a small boat with a paddle
entries.definitionCN: 用短桨划（小艇），动作相近但用具与船型不同
争吵，正式的说法，对应 row 的口语争吵义

normalIntro.en: Five ways to remember row through lines, oars and rows of seats.
normalIntro.cn: 五条围绕排列、船桨与成排座位的记忆路径。

normal.en: ROW looks like a straight line of letters, R-O-W, one after another.
normal.cn: ROW 三个字母排成一条直线，就像一排东西首尾相连。

normal.en: ROW a boat: the oar pulls the water in one long line each stroke.
normal.cn: 划船时每桨在水面拉出一道长直线，和「一排」意象相通。

normal.en: Cinema seats come in rows: front row means the closest seats.
normal.cn: 影院座位成排：front row 就是离银幕最近的前排。

normal.en: Five wins IN A ROW: think of five gold medals lined up in a row.
normal.cn: 五连胜 in a row：想象五块金牌排成一行的画面。

normal.en: ROW with two readings: /rəʊ/ for lines and boats, /raʊ/ for fights.
normal.cn: row 两种读法：/rəʊ/ 指排与划船，/raʊ/ 指吵架，靠重音区分。

abstract.en: See chairs stretch to the horizon, all standing in one endless row.
abstract.cn: 想象椅子一直排到天边，构成一条望不到头的长排。

abstract.en: Feel the oar slice the water, leaving a straight line behind the boat.
abstract.cn: 感受船桨切开水面，在船尾留下一道笔直的水线。

abstract.en: Picture medals pinned side by side, each win another item in the row.
abstract.cn: 想象奖牌一枚枚并排钉在墙上，每一枚都是这排里的一个新成员。

examples.en: The teacher asked us to stand in a row.
examples.cn: 老师让我们站成一排。

examples.en: They rowed the little boat to the other side of the river.
examples.cn: 他们把小船划到了河对岸。

examples.en: She has been late for school three days in a row.
examples.cn: 她已经连续三天上学迟到了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「肉」——一排烤肉架上一排肉，排排都是肉；row 读音近似「肉」

root: 「一排」义源自古英语 rāw（行列），属日耳曼语源；「争吵」义一般认为来源不确定，是十八世纪出现的同音异源词，两者书写混同但并非同根。

sensesIntro.en: Row moves from a straight line of things to pulling oars, to continuous wins, and to an informal quarrel.
sensesIntro.cn: row 从成排的直线出发，延伸到划船动作、连续纪录，再到口语中的争吵。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: things placed one after another in a line
core.cn: 核心意象：东西一个接一个排成的直线

branches.en: The line image covers both static rows and repeated wins.
branches.cn: 直线意象同时覆盖静止的成排与接连的胜负。

branches.en: Each oar stroke draws a line through the water.
branches.cn: 每一桨都在水面划出一道线，划船由此挂靠排列义。

branches.en: Rowing a boat and rowing crops of seats share the ordered-line feeling.
branches.cn: 划船与成排座位共享「有序直线」的语感。

branches.en: The quarrel sense is a sound-alike word, not grown from the line image.
branches.cn: 争吵义是同音异源词，并非从排列意象长出。

branches.en: Rows give order to seats, houses and shops along a street.
branches.cn: 成排给座椅、房屋与街边商店带来秩序感。

intro.en: Row builds few derivatives; most compounds keep the line or boat sense.
intro.cn: row 的派生词不多，合成词大多保留排列或划船义。

latinIntro.en: Row is Germanic in origin with no Latin relatives, so no Latin entries are listed.
latinIntro.cn: row 属日耳曼语源词，没有拉丁同族词，故不列拉丁词条。

items.example: Each rower pulls hard on the oar.

items.meaning: the sport of racing boats with oars
items.example: Rowing is popular at the university.
items.exampleCN: 划船运动在这所大学很流行。

items.meaning: a small boat moved with oars
items.example: They rented a rowboat for the afternoon.
items.exampleCN: 他们下午租了一条划艇。

items.example: He was absent twice in a row.

items.meaning: the line of seats closest to the front
items.example: The kids fought for the front row.

items.meaning: a house built in a continuous row with shared side walls
items.example: They live in a red brick row house.
items.exampleCN: 他们住在一栋红砖排屋里。

items.meaning: to make a loud fuss or quarrel
items.example: The fans kicked up a row at the referee.
items.exampleCN: 球迷们对裁判大吵大闹。

items.meaning: the part of a prison for prisoners waiting execution
items.meaningCN: 死囚区；等待处决的囚犯牢房区
items.example: The novel is set on death row.
items.exampleCN: 这部小说以死囚区为背景。

definition_en: waste material that is thrown away; things of poor quality; foolish talk or ideas
core_image: 一堆被丢弃、不再有用的东西
scene: 请把厨房里的垃圾拿出去。Please take the rubbish out of the kitchen.
sceneCN: 这里 rubbish 是「垃圾」（第 1 个义项）；句意：请把厨房里的垃圾拿出去。

senses.title: Waste material
senses.definition: waste material that is thrown away
senses.definitionCN: 被丢弃的废弃材料
senses.example: The bin was full of rubbish.
senses.exampleCN: 垃圾桶里装满了垃圾。
senses.why: The core sense is useless waste.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是无用的废弃物。

senses.title: Poor quality things
senses.definition: things that are of very poor quality
senses.definitionCN: 质量极差的东西
senses.example: The film was pure rubbish.
senses.exampleCN: 那部电影简直一无是处。
senses.why: Waste material becomes a judgment on things.
senses.whyCN: 废弃物变成了对事物的评价。

senses.title: Foolish talk
senses.definition: foolish talk or ideas
senses.definitionCN: 愚蠢的话或想法
senses.example: Don't talk rubbish about her.
senses.exampleCN: 别乱说她的是非。
senses.why: Worthless things become worthless words.
senses.whyCN: 没有价值的东西变成没有价值的话。

intro.en: Rubbish comes from Middle English robous, rubble or waste.
intro.cn: rubbish 源自中古英语 robous，意为碎石、废料。

items.en: Robous names broken stone and waste.
items.cn: robous 指碎石与废料。

items.en: Related forms describe rubble from buildings.
items.cn: 相关词形描述建筑物产生的碎石。

items.en: Rubbish broadens to household waste.
items.cn: rubbish 扩大到家庭垃圾。

items.en: Rubbish also means worthless things.
items.cn: rubbish 也指毫无价值的东西。

items.en: Talk rubbish is a common phrase.
items.cn: talk rubbish 成为常用说法。

note.en: Rubbish is waste; rubble is broken stone.
note.cn: rubbish 是垃圾，rubble 则是碎砖石。

entries.definition: to move a hand over a surface
a soft material from tree sap

normalIntro.en: Rubbish is what is thrown out or has no worth.
normalIntro.cn: rubbish 是被扔掉或没有价值的东西。

normal.en: The street was covered in rubbish after the fair.
normal.cn: 集市过后街上到处是垃圾。

normal.en: That argument is complete rubbish.
normal.cn: 那个论点完全站不住脚。

normal.en: They collect rubbish every Tuesday morning.
normal.cn: 他们每周二早上收垃圾。

normal.en: He threw the old magazines into the rubbish.
normal.cn: 他把旧杂志扔进了垃圾里。

normal.en: Do not believe the rubbish in that message.
normal.cn: 别相信那条消息里的胡话。

abstract.en: Picture a bin overflowing at the curb.
abstract.cn: 想象路边一个满溢的垃圾桶。

abstract.en: Imagine torn paper blowing across a yard.
abstract.cn: 想象碎纸在院子里被风吹动。

abstract.en: Think of words that fall apart as you hear them.
abstract.cn: 想象一些话一听就站不住脚。

examples.en: The council collects household rubbish on Mondays.
examples.cn: 市政部门每周一收集生活垃圾。

examples.en: The film was dismissed as rubbish by critics.
examples.cn: 评论家斥那部电影为垃圾。

examples.en: He talks rubbish when he is nervous.
examples.cn: 他一紧张就胡说八道。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「rubbish」读起来像「垃圾堆里拉比什」，可以联想一袋被人丢弃的垃圾。

root: 中古英语 robous（碎石、废料）进入英语后扩展为「垃圾、废物、废话」。

sensesIntro.en: Rubbish means waste material, things of poor quality, or foolish talk.
sensesIntro.cn: rubbish 意为废弃物、劣质东西，或废话。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a heap of things thrown away.
core.cn: 核心意象：一堆被丢弃的东西。

branches.en: The base sense is physical waste.
branches.cn: 基础义是实体的废弃物。

branches.en: Waste becomes a judgment of quality.
branches.cn: 废弃物变成对质量的判断。

branches.en: Worthless things become worthless words.
branches.cn: 无价值之物变成无价值之言。

branches.en: Physical and figurative waste share worthlessness.
branches.cn: 实体垃圾与比喻性垃圾都指没有价值。

branches.en: Bad products and bad talk are both dismissed.
branches.cn: 劣质产品与胡言乱语都会被否定。

intro.en: Rubbish is an old English word without a Latin root.
intro.cn: rubbish 是古老的英语词，没有拉丁词根。

latinIntro.en: Rubbish has no Latin root; it comes from Middle English.
latinIntro.cn: rubbish 没有拉丁词根，它来自中古英语。

items.example: Robous is the earliest recorded form.
items.exampleCN: robous 是最早有记载的形式。

items.example: Rubbish keeps the sense of waste.

items.exampleCN: rubbishy 形容廉价劣质的东西。

items.example: Bin forms the compound rubbish bin.
items.exampleCN: bin 构成复合词 rubbish bin。

items.example: Dump forms the compound rubbish dump.
items.exampleCN: dump 构成复合词 rubbish dump。

definition_en: not polite; offensive or insulting; roughly made or simple
core_image: 未经打磨的粗糙表面，欠缺应有的礼数
scene: 对服务员大喊大叫是很无礼的。Shouting at the waiter is very rude.
sceneCN: 这里 rude 是「无礼的」（第 1 个义项）；句意：对服务员大喊大叫是很无礼的。

senses.title: Not polite
senses.definition: not polite in behavior or speech
senses.definitionCN: 言行上不礼貌的
senses.example: It is rude to interrupt.
senses.exampleCN: 打断别人说话是不礼貌的。
senses.why: The core sense is a lack of polish.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是欠缺应有的修养。

senses.title: Offensive
senses.definition: offensive or insulting in an obvious way
senses.definitionCN: 明显冒犯或侮辱人的
senses.example: He made a rude gesture.
senses.exampleCN: 他做了个粗鲁的手势。
senses.why: Impoliteness hardens into open offence.
senses.whyCN: 不礼貌固化为公开冒犯。

senses.title: Roughly made
senses.definition: roughly made or simple in a primitive way
senses.definitionCN: 制作粗糙或原始简朴的
senses.example: They sheltered in a rude wooden hut.
senses.exampleCN: 他们躲在一间简陋的木屋里。
senses.why: The old sense is raw and unformed.
senses.whyCN: 旧义是未经加工、粗糙的。

intro.en: Rude comes from Latin rudis, raw and unformed.
intro.cn: rude 源自拉丁语 rudis，意为原始、未加工的。

items.en: Rudis means raw or rough.
items.cn: rudis 意为生的、粗糙的。

items.en: Rude keeps the sense of roughness.
items.cn: rude 保留粗糙的含义。

items.en: Rude describes rough work or manners.
items.cn: rude 形容粗糙的作品或举止。

items.en: Rude shifts toward social impoliteness.
items.cn: rude 转向指社交上的不礼貌。

items.en: Rude mainly means impolite today.
items.cn: 如今 rude 主要表示不礼貌。

note.en: Rude is impolite; crude is rough or unrefined.
note.cn: rude 是不礼貌，crude 则是粗制或粗俗。

entries.definition: a statement of what is allowed

normalIntro.en: Rude is unpolished, either in manners or in form.
normalIntro.cn: rude 是未经打磨，既指礼数也指做工。

normal.en: It is rude to point at people.
normal.cn: 用手指人是不礼貌的。

normal.en: She was rude to the driver for no reason.
normal.cn: 她无缘无故对司机无礼。

normal.en: The visitors made rude comments about the food.
normal.cn: 客人们对食物说了些粗鲁的话。

normal.en: They built a rude shelter from branches.
normal.cn: 他们用树枝搭了个简陋的棚子。

normal.en: His rude awakening came when the bill arrived.
normal.cn: 账单寄来时他才猛然醒悟。

abstract.en: Picture a rough stone never polished smooth.
abstract.cn: 想象一块从未打磨光滑的石头。

abstract.en: Imagine a door slammed in someone's face.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇门当着人的面被摔上。

abstract.en: Think of a hut made from loose branches.
abstract.cn: 想象一间用松散树枝搭成的小屋。

examples.en: The clerk was rude to every customer.
examples.cn: 那名店员对每位顾客都很无礼。

examples.en: He apologized for his rude remarks.
examples.cn: 他为自己的无礼言论道歉。

examples.en: They slept in a rude hut near the river.
examples.cn: 他们睡在河边一间简陋的木屋里。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「rude」读音像「鲁的」：言行鲁莽无礼，就是「粗鲁的」。

root: 拉丁语 rudis（生的、未加工的）经古法语进入英语，核心义「未经打磨」，由物及人引申为「无礼」。

sensesIntro.en: Rude means impolite, openly offensive, or roughly and simply made.
sensesIntro.cn: rude 意为不礼貌的、公然冒犯的，或制作粗糙简朴的。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a rough surface with no polish.
core.cn: 核心意象：没有打磨过的粗糙表面。

branches.en: The base sense is a lack of good manners.
branches.cn: 基础义是缺乏礼貌。

branches.en: Impoliteness becomes open offence.
branches.cn: 不礼貌变成公然冒犯。

branches.en: The old sense of roughness survives in objects.
branches.cn: 「粗糙」的旧义仍保留在物品上。

branches.en: Both concern behavior that harms others.
branches.cn: 两者都涉及伤害他人的行为。

branches.en: Unpolished manners and unpolished wood pair up.
branches.cn: 未修饰的举止与未打磨的木头相互对应。

intro.en: Rude comes from Latin rudis without a prefix.
intro.cn: rude 来自拉丁语 rudis，不带前缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin rudis is the direct source of rude.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 rudis 是 rude 的直接来源。

items.example: Rudis is the source of rude.
items.exampleCN: rudis 是 rude 的来源。

items.example: Rude keeps the sense of roughness.

definition_en: an official statement of what is allowed; control by a government or person; to govern; to decide officially
core_image: 一根笔直的尺子，划出能做与不能做的界线
scene: 学校对手机使用有严格的规定。The school has a strict rule about phones.
sceneCN: 这里 rule 是「规定、规则」（第 1 个义项）；句意：学校对手机使用有严格的规定。

senses.title: Official statement
senses.definition: an official statement of what is allowed or required
senses.definitionCN: 规定允许或要求什么的正式条文
senses.example: The first rule is to arrive on time.
senses.exampleCN: 第一条规则是准时到达。
senses.why: The core sense is a straight standard.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是一条笔直的标准线。

senses.title: Control by a ruler
senses.definition: control by a government or a person
senses.definitionCN: 政府或个人的控制
senses.example: The island was under foreign rule for years.
senses.exampleCN: 这个岛曾被外国统治多年。
senses.why: A standard of behavior becomes control of people.
senses.whyCN: 行为标准变成对人的控制。

senses.title: To govern
senses.definition: to govern a country or group
senses.definitionCN: 统治一个国家或群体
senses.example: The queen ruled for forty years.
senses.exampleCN: 女王统治了四十年。
senses.why: The noun of control becomes the verb of controlling.
senses.whyCN: 控制的名词变成控制的动词。

senses.title: Decide officially
senses.definition: to decide an official question
senses.definitionCN: 对正式问题作出裁决
senses.example: The judge ruled in her favor.
senses.exampleCN: 法官判她胜诉。
senses.why: Setting a standard becomes giving a verdict.
senses.whyCN: 设定标准变成作出裁决。

intro.en: Rule comes from Latin regula, a straight stick or standard.
intro.cn: rule 源自拉丁语 regula，意为直尺或标准。

items.en: Regula means a straight stick.
items.cn: regula 意为笔直的杆或尺。

items.en: Regere means to guide or keep straight.
items.cn: regere 意为引导、使笔直。

items.en: Riule means a rule or order.
items.cn: riu le 意为规则或命令。

items.en: Rule covers standards and government.
items.cn: rule 兼指标准与统治。

items.en: Rule also means to give a decision.
items.cn: rule 还表示作出裁定。

note.en: A rule is a standard; a ruse is a trick.
note.cn: rule 是规则，ruse 则是计谋。

entries.definition: a rule made by a government

normalIntro.en: A rule draws a line and keeps people inside it.
normalIntro.cn: rule 划出一条界线，把人约束在其中。

normal.en: The club has a rule against smoking.
normal.cn: 俱乐部有禁止吸烟的规定。

normal.en: The emperor ruled the land for many years.
normal.cn: 皇帝统治这片土地多年。

normal.en: The court ruled that the arrest was illegal.
normal.cn: 法院裁定这次逮捕不合法。

normal.en: As a rule, she walks to work.
normal.cn: 通常她步行上班。

normal.en: Doctors ruled out a broken bone.
normal.cn: 医生排除了骨折的可能。

abstract.en: Picture a ruler drawing one firm straight line.
abstract.cn: 想象一把尺子画出一条笔直的线。

abstract.en: Imagine a crown placed over a map.
abstract.cn: 想象一顶王冠压在地图上。

abstract.en: Think of a judge's hammer setting a boundary.
abstract.cn: 想象法官的木槌划出边界。

examples.en: Every game needs clear rules.
examples.cn: 每项游戏都需要明确的规则。

examples.en: The small kingdom was ruled by one family.
examples.cn: 这个小王国由一个家族统治。

examples.en: The committee ruled that the plan could proceed.
examples.cn: 委员会裁定该计划可以继续。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「rule」与 ruler（尺子）同源：用尺子划出界线，就是「规则」；拿着尺子管人，就是「统治」。

root: 拉丁语 regula（直尺、标准）来自 regere（使笔直、引导），核心义「划出直线、立下标准」，再引申为统治与裁定。

sensesIntro.en: Rule means a regulation, control by a government, to govern, or to decide officially.
sensesIntro.cn: rule 意为规则、统治、治理，或正式裁定。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a straight stick drawing a limit.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根直尺划出界限。

branches.en: The base sense is a standard or regulation.
branches.cn: 基础义是标准或规则。

branches.en: A standard becomes control over people.
branches.cn: 标准变成对人的控制。

branches.en: Control becomes the verb to govern.
branches.cn: 控制变成表示统治的动词。

branches.en: Setting a standard becomes issuing a verdict.
branches.cn: 设定标准变成作出裁决。

branches.en: Rules guide both daily life and courts.
branches.cn: 规则既指导日常也指导法庭。

intro.en: Rule comes from Latin regula, a straight measure.
intro.cn: rule 来自拉丁语 regula，意为直尺。

latinIntro.en: Latin regula and regere supply the core forms.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 regula 与 regere 提供核心词形。

items.example: Regula is the direct source of rule.
items.exampleCN: regula 是 rule 的直接来源。

items.example: Regere gives the sense of guiding.

items.meaning: a measuring stick or a governor
items.example: Ruler adds the person or tool ending.
items.exampleCN: ruler 加上了表示人或工具的结尾。

latinEntries.exampleCN: regere 是表示引导的动词。

definition_en: a straight strip used for measuring and drawing lines; a person who governs a country; someone who controls a group
core_image: 一根笔直、带刻度的长条，或手持权杖发号施令的人
scene: 他用尺子画了一条笔直的线。He used a ruler to draw a straight line.
sceneCN: 这里 ruler 是「尺子」（第 1 个义项）；句意：他用尺子画了一条笔直的线。

senses.title: Measuring strip
senses.definition: a straight strip used for measuring and drawing lines
senses.definitionCN: 用来测量和画线的直条
senses.example: Use a ruler to draw a straight line.
senses.exampleCN: 用尺子画一条直线。
senses.why: The core tool is a straight measure.
senses.whyCN: 核心工具是笔直的测量条。

senses.title: Person who governs
senses.definition: a person who governs a country
senses.definitionCN: 统治一个国家的人
senses.example: The ruler of the small kingdom was kind.
senses.exampleCN: 这个小王国的统治者很仁慈。
senses.why: The straight standard becomes the person who sets it.
senses.whyCN: 画标准的人变成了设定标准的人。

senses.title: Controller of a group
senses.definition: someone who controls a group or situation
senses.definitionCN: 控制一个群体或局面的人
senses.example: She was the real ruler of the household.
senses.exampleCN: 她才是这个家真正的掌权者。
senses.why: Political control extends to daily life.
senses.whyCN: 政治上的控制扩展到日常生活。

intro.en: Ruler is rule plus the person suffix -er.
intro.cn: ruler 是 rule 加表示人的后缀 -er。

items.en: Regula means a straight stick.
items.cn: regula 意为直尺。

items.en: Riule keeps the sense of a standard.
items.cn: riu le 保留标准之义。

items.en: Rule covers measuring and governing.
items.cn: rule 兼指测量与统治。

items.en: -Er forms the person or tool noun.
items.cn: -er 构成表示人或工具的名词。

items.en: Ruler names both a stick and a governor.
items.cn: ruler 同时指尺子和统治者。

note.en: A ruler measures or governs; a rule is the standard itself.
note.cn: ruler 是尺子或统治者，rule 则是标准本身。

entries.definition: an official who governs a region

normalIntro.en: A ruler can be a straight measuring tool or a governing person.
normalIntro.cn: ruler 既可以是笔直的测量工具，也可以是治理者。

normal.en: The ruler on my desk is made of steel.
normal.cn: 我桌上的尺子是钢制的。

normal.en: The ruler ordered a new road to be built.
normal.cn: 统治者下令修建一条新路。

normal.en: Children use rulers to draw neat lines.
normal.cn: 孩子们用尺子画整齐的线。

normal.en: The old ruler was loved by the people.
normal.cn: 那位老君主受到人民爱戴。

normal.en: He is the ruler of the chess club.
normal.cn: 他是这个棋社的掌权者。

abstract.en: Picture a steel strip with numbered marks.
abstract.cn: 想象一根带刻度的钢条。

abstract.en: Imagine a crown resting on a map.
abstract.cn: 想象一顶王冠放在地图上。

abstract.en: Think of a hand holding both a pen and a staff.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手同时握着笔和权杖。

examples.en: The line was drawn without a ruler.
examples.cn: 这条线不是用尺子画的。

examples.en: The ruler promised lower taxes.
examples.cn: 统治者承诺降低税收。

examples.en: Each ruler of the region left a mark on the city.
examples.cn: 这个地区的每一位统治者都在城中留下印记。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「ruler」是 rule（规则）加 -er：定规则的工具是「尺子」，定规则的人是「统治者」。

root: 由 rule（规则、直尺）加 -er 构成，rule 源自拉丁语 regula（直尺、标准）。

sensesIntro.en: Ruler means a measuring strip, a person who governs, or someone who controls a group.
sensesIntro.cn: ruler 意为测量用的直尺、治理国家的人，或控制群体的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a straight measure or the person behind it.
core.cn: 核心意象：笔直的测量物，或设定标准的人。

branches.en: The base sense is the measuring tool.
branches.cn: 基础义是测量工具。

branches.en: The standard becomes a governing person.
branches.cn: 标准变成治理者。

branches.en: Political control extends to daily groups.
branches.cn: 政治控制扩展到日常群体。

branches.en: Tool and governor share the same old root.
branches.cn: 工具与统治者共享同一古老词根。

branches.en: A monarch and a household head both rule.
branches.cn: 君主与一家之主都在治理。

intro.en: Ruler is rule plus the agent suffix -er.
intro.cn: ruler 是 rule 加施事后缀 -er。

latinIntro.en: Latin regula is the root of rule and ruler.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 regula 是 rule 与 ruler 的词根。

items.example: Ruling comes from the verb rule.

definition_en: to move quickly on foot; to operate or function; to manage a business; a period of activity
core_image: 脚步不停向前，机器不停转动
scene: 他每天清晨沿着河边跑步。He runs along the river every morning.
sceneCN: 这里 run 是「跑」（第 1 个义项）；句意：他每天清晨沿着河边跑步。

senses.title: Move fast on foot
senses.definition: to move quickly on foot
senses.definitionCN: 用双脚快速移动
senses.example: She runs every morning before work.
senses.exampleCN: 她每天上班前都跑步。
senses.why: The core sense is fast forward motion.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是快速的向前运动。

senses.title: Operate
senses.definition: to operate or function
senses.definitionCN: 运作或发挥功能
senses.example: The engine runs on diesel.
senses.exampleCN: 这台发动机靠柴油运转。
senses.why: Legs moving becomes a machine moving.
senses.whyCN: 双腿的跑动变成机器的运转。

senses.title: Manage
senses.definition: to manage or control a business
senses.definitionCN: 经营或管理一项业务
senses.example: He runs a small café near the station.
senses.exampleCN: 他在车站附近经营一家小咖啡馆。
senses.why: Keeping something moving becomes managing it.
senses.whyCN: 让事物持续运转变成管理它。

senses.title: Period of activity
senses.definition: a period during which something operates or continues
senses.definitionCN: 某事运作或持续的时期
senses.example: The play had a long run in the city.
senses.exampleCN: 这部戏在这座城市长期上演。
senses.why: The action becomes a stretch of time.
senses.whyCN: 动作变成一段时间。

intro.en: Run comes from Old English rinnan, to flow or run.
intro.cn: run 源自古英语 rinnan，意为流动、奔跑。

items.en: Rinnan means to flow or move quickly.
items.cn: rinnan 意为流动或快速移动。

items.en: Rinna reinforces the sense of flowing.
items.cn: rinna 强化了流动之义。

items.en: Runnen covers people, water, and machines.
items.cn: runnen 兼指人、水与机器。

items.en: Run extends to managing a business.
items.cn: run 扩展到经营企业。

items.en: In the long run becomes a fixed phrase.
items.cn: in the long run 成为固定搭配。

note.en: Run is fast movement; ruin is destruction.
note.cn: run 是快速移动，ruin 则是毁灭。

entries.definition: a strap for controlling a horse
to run very fast for a short distance
to work or make something work
to control a business or group

normalIntro.en: Run is anything moving onward without stopping.
normalIntro.cn: run 是任何持续向前运转的事物。

normal.en: The children ran across the field.
normal.cn: 孩子们跑过田野。

normal.en: The machine runs all night.
normal.cn: 机器整夜运转。

normal.en: She runs a bookshop on the corner.
normal.cn: 她在街角经营一家书店。

normal.en: We ran out of milk this morning.
normal.cn: 今天早上我们的牛奶用完了。

normal.en: The show had a successful run.
normal.cn: 这部演出连续上演很成功。

abstract.en: Picture feet hitting the ground in rhythm.
abstract.cn: 想象双脚有节奏地踏地。

abstract.en: Imagine wheels turning without pause.
abstract.cn: 想象车轮不停转动。

abstract.en: Think of a river flowing past a town.
abstract.cn: 想象一条河从城镇旁流过。

examples.en: He ran to catch the last bus.
examples.cn: 他跑去赶末班车。

examples.en: The factory runs day and night.
examples.cn: 这家工厂昼夜运转。

examples.en: They run a farm outside the city.
examples.cn: 他们在城外经营一座农场。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「run」读音短促，像脚步快速点地：跑起来，机器也跟着转起来。

root: 古英语 rinnan（流动、奔跑）经中古英语 runnen 演变为「跑、运转、经营」，核心义「持续向前」。

sensesIntro.en: Run means to move fast on foot, to operate, to manage, or a period of activity.
sensesIntro.cn: run 意为奔跑、运转、经营，或一段活动时期。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: steady forward motion.
core.cn: 核心意象：持续向前的运动。

branches.en: The base sense is fast movement on foot.
branches.cn: 基础义是快速跑动。

branches.en: Human running becomes machine operation.
branches.cn: 人的跑动变成机器运转。

branches.en: Keeping things moving becomes managing.
branches.cn: 让事物运转变成经营管理。

branches.en: The action becomes a stretch of time.
branches.cn: 动作变成一段时间。

branches.en: Machines and businesses both keep running.
branches.cn: 机器与企业都需要持续运转。

intro.en: Run is an Old English verb with many related forms.
intro.cn: run 是古英语动词，衍生形式很多。

latinIntro.en: Run has no Latin root; it is Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: run 没有拉丁词根，属于日耳曼语族。

items.exampleCN: runs 是现在时单数形式。

definition_en: a person who runs; a person taking part in a race; someone who carries goods illegally
core_image: 一双不停向前迈步的腿
scene: 这名跑者在最后一圈超过了所有人。The runner passed everyone on the final lap.
sceneCN: 这里 runner 是「赛跑者」（第 2 个义项）；句意：这名跑者在最后一圈超过了所有人。

senses.title: Person who runs
senses.definition: a person who runs
senses.definitionCN: 跑步的人
senses.example: A runner passed us on the hill.
senses.exampleCN: 一个跑步的人在山坡上超过了我们。
senses.why: The base sense adds a person to run.
senses.whyCN: 基础义是在 run 后加上人。

senses.title: Race competitor
senses.definition: a person taking part in a race
senses.definitionCN: 参加赛跑的选手
senses.example: The runner finished second.
senses.exampleCN: 这位赛跑者获得了第二。
senses.why: Running becomes an organized contest.
senses.whyCN: 跑步变成有组织的比赛。

senses.title: Illegal courier
senses.definition: someone who carries goods illegally
senses.definitionCN: 非法运送货物的人
senses.example: Police stopped a drug runner at the border.
senses.exampleCN: 警方在边境拦下了一名毒品走私者。
senses.why: Carrying things quickly becomes smuggling.
senses.whyCN: 快速运送东西变成走私。

intro.en: Runner is run plus the person suffix -er.
intro.cn: runner 是 run 加表示人的后缀 -er。

items.en: Rinnan means to flow or run.
items.cn: rinnan 意为流动或奔跑。

items.en: Runnen covers people and water.
items.cn: runnen 兼指人与水。

items.en: -Er forms the person who runs.
items.cn: -er 构成跑步的人。

items.en: Runner also names a race competitor.
items.cn: runner 也指赛跑选手。

items.en: Runner extends to illegal couriers.
items.cn: runner 扩展到非法运送者。

note.en: A runner runs; a ruler measures or governs.
note.cn: runner 是跑步的人，ruler 则是尺子或统治者。

entries.definition: someone who runs slowly for exercise
someone who carries messages or goods

normalIntro.en: A runner is a person whose job or sport is running.
normalIntro.cn: runner 是以跑步为运动或职业的人。

normal.en: The runner trained for the city race.
normal.cn: 这名跑者为城市赛跑训练。

normal.en: A tired runner stopped at the water station.
normal.cn: 一名疲惫的跑者在补水站停下。

normal.en: She is the fastest runner in her class.
normal.cn: 她是班上跑得最快的人。

normal.en: The runner-up received a silver medal.
normal.cn: 亚军获得了一枚银牌。

normal.en: The police caught the runner at the port.
normal.cn: 警方在港口抓住了那名走私者。

abstract.en: Picture legs moving in a steady rhythm.
abstract.cn: 想象双腿以稳定节奏迈动。

abstract.en: Imagine a number on a runner's chest.
abstract.cn: 想象跑者胸前别着号码布。

abstract.en: Think of a parcel passed quickly in the dark.
abstract.cn: 想象一个包裹在暗处被快速传递。

examples.en: The runner broke the record by two seconds.
examples.cn: 这名赛跑者以两秒之差打破了纪录。

examples.en: A runner delivered the message before dawn.
examples.cn: 一名信使在黎明前送出了消息。

examples.en: Runners gathered at the start line.
examples.cn: 跑者们聚集在起跑线。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「runner」是 run（跑）加 -er：不停跑动的人，就是「跑步者、赛跑者」。

root: 由 run（跑）加施事后缀 -er 构成，run 源自古英语 rinnan（流动、奔跑）。

sensesIntro.en: Runner means a person who runs, a race competitor, or someone who carries goods illegally.
sensesIntro.cn: runner 意为跑步的人、赛跑选手，或非法运送货物的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person in constant forward motion.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个持续向前奔跑的人。

branches.en: The base sense is a person who runs.
branches.cn: 基础义是跑步的人。

branches.en: Running becomes an organized race.
branches.cn: 跑步变成有组织的比赛。

branches.en: Fast carrying becomes smuggling.
branches.cn: 快速运送变成走私。

branches.en: Every racer is first a runner.
branches.cn: 每位赛跑者首先都是跑步的人。

branches.en: Race and illegal delivery both involve speed.
branches.cn: 赛跑与非法运送都强调速度。

intro.en: Runner is run plus the agent suffix -er.
intro.cn: runner 是 run 加施事后缀 -er。

latinIntro.en: Runner has no Latin root; run is Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: runner 没有拉丁词根，run 属于日耳曼语族。
